Review Title: Excellent for what it is, but too twisted and unpleasant
Review: Dark Knight is without a doubt a very well made movie and will please most all of the adult fans' of Batman. However, I for one am greatly disturbed by the content of a movie that will inevitably be viewed by most teenage boys and many children given that the main character is a very popular comic book hero. Heck, I had to look away during a number of scenes. To give this movie a PG-13 might seem appropriate when compared to the ratings given to other recent movies, but this movie contains many, many scenes which are waaaaaaay too dark, sadistic, and disturbing for really anyone under 18 in my opinion. The makers of this movie wisely removed all traces of blood from the movie to appease the rating system, but come on, twisted serial-killer kind of horrific violence and terror (and lots of it) doesn't depend on the appearance of blood to be highly disturbing, especially to young children. If children today aren't disturbed by what they see in the Dark Knight, then that would help explain how events like Colombine can happen. So if you haven't already routinely exposed your children to the darkest of depraved movie characters (a la Silence of the Lambs), then PLEASE think twice about letting them see this movie. It's screen time is composed of 90% sick violence and 10% positive message.

Review Title: A Pinnacle in Film making history
Review: Let me get one thing straight, I've never liked Batman. Before Batman Begins, Batman was literally a joke, a meme. But Nolan's Batman Begins came out and crashed theaters everywhere. It became one of the most popular movies of the year and for good reason. Nolan had set a high bar with Batman Begins and anything below that bar with the Dark Knight would be rejected. And he didn't disappoint. The Dark Knight is one of the most intriguing movies I've seen to date. I've seen good and bad and I can tell you. The Dark Knight is a true masterpiece. I would've rated this 10 but my philosophy is that every movie can be made better, there is no perfect movie. So I'm not rating the Dark Knight a ten. But the Dark Knight is one of those few movies which is flat on close to near perfect. It's an intense and thrilling movie that will get you on the edge of your seat in the theaters. Not to mention, the acting is absolutely superb. The late Heath Ledger's performance is to die for in this movie. His portrayal of the Joker remains to date some of the best acting the world has seen and in my opinion the best I've ever seen. The storyline is gripping and character development is off the roof. The casting is perfect with Bale's batman adding his dark and serious tone to the movie. The Dark Knight is filled with moments you can remember for years on end. There are very few minor problems with the movie itself, but it's all minor compared to the satisfaction you'll receive while watching the Dark Knight. The ending is truly spectacular. I do have to say, The Dark Knight is a fairly dark movie and many do not appreciate this dark approach that Nolan took, but I have to say. The Dark Knight is probably the second best movie I've seen by far next to Inception.

Review Title: Sequels just cannot surpass the original...or can they?
Review: Goadfather Part 2 couldn't do it. Aliens couldn't do it. Die hard couldn't do it. Did Dark Knight repeat the history or made one? I think the latter one. I wanted to see this movie right from the start of the year. This indeed was the most awaited movie for a long time at least for me. When I left the cinema I surely was spell bounded. I am not actually a fan of action movies, rather I hate them. Very few have made it to my top list. Main reason about disliking action movies is that in most of them there is little or no character development and now-a-days they rely heavily on the CGI and stuff like that. Very little heed is actually paid in the 'acting' department.But Batman Begins and The Dark Knight have surely changed my views. I guess if give a talented artist like Nolan any previous crap, he can turn it into a masterpiece. The Character Development in both the movies was something I have never seen in an action movie.Talking about The Dark Knight, well the movie was the most talked about in a long time. And seeing it just the next day after 'Hancock' made me realize that between two action movies many things are common but in a very rare case like this one a hell lot of things can be different. The Dark Knight scores on every front.Direction. Well when 'Begins' was in the making I had doubted Nolan had turned commercial after agreeing to direct a previously 'failed' series. But to everyone's astonishment as I mentioned above he did manage to turn a crap of a series into a masterpiece. And this time too he manages to accomplish the same rather couple of steps ahead than his previous attempt. His direction is simply magnificent. He gives the film its dark nature which is what a Batman movie should have. He never overemphasizes on any of the character. Each character from Joker to Two face gets his due.The special effects. Well I have to say that most of the stunts, car chases in the movie seem very real. Well most of them are actually real. The fact I liked here is that the film does not try to attract the audiences by the overuse of CGI as in the case of 'Spiderman' series. The film has its very own soul and does not have to rely on these factors. The car chase seen in the tunnel was one of the best. A film should never rely heavily on the CGI as the techniques continue to get better and better and after 20 years those CGIs will be worth laughing . Believe me after 50 years or so people would be laughing on the matrix series not for its philosophical subtext but for its action scenes while on the other 'Godfather' will still be considered a masterpiece. Cinematography. Well thats something I really don't appreciate in action movies. 'Bourne' series' cinematography was a pain in the neck. The Dark Knight's film-noir inspired cinematography will certainly set new standards for action films to come in years. Music. Well the trademark music(I'm talking about the one which appears just for a second in the last track of the official soundtrack but is present in both the movies more as a background score) by Hans Zimmer & James Newton Howard is just fantastic. They delivered the best at the right moments in the movie. None of the tracks overshadowed the action. Nor did it distract the audience from the plot. Perhaps the Best soundtrack to come in years.Acting. In this department Heath Ledger steals the show. May be he will be the second actor after peter finch to win Oscar posthumously. While the joker is presented like never before, the film does not lose the emphasis on other characters. Even the cop in the interrogation room with joker has a pivotal role. Bale does justice with his character. Caine like in the first movie is excellent in his supporting role. Morgan Freemann though in a small role is not disappointing. Aaron Eckhart's character's change from Harvey Dent to Two Face is shown steadily and progressively in a very believable manner. Gary Oldman as Lt. Gordan also brings quite a lot of surprises in the movie. His dialogs during the end of the movie were fantastic. Only disappointment was Maggie Gyllenhaal in the role of Rachel. She does not seem to be too important to the script. This is the only flaw I can find in the film. Finally this is one of those masterpieces not difficult but impossible to make. An action genre movie appealing to the audiences of every genre. Such movies will come only once in a long long time. Action movies are always rejected by the Oscars. Will this movie make history?

I firmly believe that The Dark Knight is in the discussion of the top twenty-five greatest movies ever made. This movie is Star Wars for a new generation. This movie is lightning in a bottle.From the word go, we are treated to a taut, suspenseful heist sequence with all kinds of reversals and double-crosses. Within the first minute you notice something about this movie: it feels larger than life. It's crackling with energy and movement, bursting with fantastic scenes, great dialogue, tight editing, and outstanding performances. One of those performances is surely in the top ten male leads of all time, and you know the one I'm talking about. Heath Ledger as the Joker is pure electricity. He's funny, psychotic, dangerous, wildly unpredictable, full of tics and utterly enthralling to watch. The supporting cast is where I somewhat sense a flaw or two. Christian Bale is much better playing Bruce Wayne then he is behind the mask. Maggie Gyllenhaal and Aaron Eckhart are just serviceable. However, Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman turn in great work in their minor parts.The plot never stops moving, not once loses steam. The Joker is terrorizing Gotham City, and it's up to Batman to stop him. It's an ever-escalating series of stakes, paced to perfection. The action sequences are heart-pounding. The music flows well with the action on screen. Jonathan Nolan's dialogue is smart and memorable.Very few movies have come together so powerfully and so well, in all departments. The closest analogy I can think of is that The Dark Knight is the Citizen Kane of superhero movies. Both give you the continual sense that you are watching a great film. Although, where Kane was lauded for its brand new innovations in film technique, The Dark Knight deserves praise for taking the blockbuster genre to near-perfection. 9.5/10

The film is very entertaining in my eyes, but did not excite me as much as Batman 89 and Batman begins.

Review Title: One of the best films ever made.
Review: I'm not easily impressed by films and do not give 10/10s out to many, but this film truly is THE best action/thriller i've ever seen and deserves MORE than a 10.Firstly, this is not a short movie being nearly 2 and a half hours long, but NEVER are you left feeling bored. Literally, from when the movie starts your into the action and never leave it. The action scenes are very good yes, but any movie can have action. Between the action your still left on the edge of your seat, eyes glued to the screen because the plot has such depth and the acting done so brilliantly. Halfway through, I picked up my remote thinking that the movie was coming to a close and happily found out that there was another HOUR left.The plot was written very well, i won't go into too much detail, but it is VERY dark and bleak and full of twists and turns that will keep you entertained for every second of those 2 and a half hours. The visuals were AMAZING, i actually found myself gasping at the breathtaking beauty of it all. I think the music was put together very well, my favourite example of this is Harvey Dent and Jimmy Gordon's scene near the end, the music created so much tension, i actually found myself not breathing it was just cinema perfection.Then there is Heath Ledger's legendary performance as The Joker. I actually struggle to find words to describe what a good job he did at portraying this evil, insane and sadistic villain. Its the little things he did like the weird little facial expressions and clicking his tongue when he was talking that made his performance so exceptional. This was his parting gift to us, and let me say he left us on a BIG high. RIP Heath Ledger, your contribution to this epic movie will never be forgotten.The supporting actors did fantastic jobs as well, veterans like Morgan Freeman and Micheal Caine. Aaron Eckhart, Maggie Gyllenhaal and Gary Oldman were all excellent. And i have to name my favourite young actor of all time, he only had a small part in this movie, but still managed to show excellence. His name is Nathan Gamble, this kid really is something else and he brought a little something extra to the already awesome movie.Batman Begins was a very good film, but this well and truly trumps it in every department. I have said 'awesome' multiple times but there really isn't words powerful enough to describe how good this film is. If you haven't seen it, DON'T rent it, but buy it and you'll be amazed just like i was.10/10 everyday, Christopher Nolan has his work cut out to make the second sequel better than this...

I came out of the theater for only the second time in my life (Pan's Labyrinth, being the other) feeling that I needed to just stay in the theater and wait for the next showing. One viewing was simply not enough to let everything sink in. It was a stunned feeling, something of awe. The people I went with kept asking me what I thought of the movie, of Ledger, and all I could do was give them one-word answers because, beyond that, I found myself at a loss for words. The 10 star rating is not for a perfect film, because no film is. It is for the audaciousness, the guts, the balls that Nolan and Co. had to do a film of this stature inside the confines of the Comic Book Movie. Iron Man is a very good film, a fun film that takes no steps outside itself, except in modernizing it for adaptation. It's clever and perky and one of my favorites of its genre. But to put it up to this is to see an ugly stepsister compared with Cinderella; it's what's at the core, which is truly important. What we have with The Dark Knight then, is something which at once is a film about a caped man, posing as a bat, who's out for justice, and also a multi-layered commentary on the world around us - "deep" may be an overstatement, but "concentrated" seems to fit. Not even the best of dramas that Hollywood puts out each year conveys complexity so cohesively, succinctly, and aesthetically. Each aspect of the film is high powered, high velocity, full of octane. The acting, from each person of the ensemble, is pitch-perfect (except for maybe Gyllenhaal who doesn't really have a whole lot to work with, but does the best job possible). Bale's ultra-conflicted Bruce Wayne is something to behold. To this day, I do not understand why people have still not caught onto his bandwagon. (He has to be one of the best actors working today without an Oscar nod.) His role may be part of the ensemble this time, but you can't help but feel the weight of his character as the story moves along; his gravitas is even more apparent the second time around. Eckhart excels as Harvey Dent, a character you really believe in as the good guy. He sees/trusts in the good of each person, that the corrupt ones can somehow be put out of their misery, and he makes us believe that he can do that. He's just a regular guy out to the save the world. The transformation to Two Face, though, I didn't feel quite worked 100% of the time, it seemed emptier, in a sense, than Dent. The revenge factor didn't seem to be enough to warrant the kind of violence he brings forth. Pivotal as that may be, it's only a minor complaint - in my opinion - in reference to the whole film. Oldman, Caine, and Freeman again deliver exactly was is asked of them and really feel like Batman's psychiatry team, just trying to keep him going, "having him endure" as Alfred says. Freeman has most of the (very few) light moments, and each provide welcome smiles and some chuckles. Caine's character Alfred is almost like Wayne's guru, giving him advice every time they speak. As well, Oldman playing Gordon, a routine good guy, is just so nice to see (again). His work is effortless; he's the treasure in these two movies nobody recognizes. To see Ledger in his last fully completed role was to see validation of what I'd been hoping: an actor going out of his way to make a character jump out on the screen and live in the hearts and minds (psyche, more like it here) of their audience. (To be frank, it doesn't happen too often.) The character of the Joker makes you laugh and, at the same time, strikes a chord: Is he meant to be just scary? Is he meant to be funny? Is he actually conveying truth? Just as Nolan shows gall in his vision, so does Ledger in his final full performance: the laugh, the voice, the constant marauding of his lips like a rabid dog, his stature, even the makeup. All of this comes together creating a theatrical show of torment, mayhem, and death; and it's all to the Joker's utter delight. When it's over, we're begging for a second act. It's too bad it can never come. Everything about this performance screams "Iconic." Hopefully, awards will follow suit. The other winners here are first, the cinematography, which gives the film it's wonderful noir quality in blues, greens and browns. Second, is the music which is fantastic again as both composers give the film even more muscle to its spectacular action scenes. The theme from Batman Begins is expanded upon and, thus, makes it feel as though it is variation B in the Batman Symphony. The final nod goes to the IMAX shots which are just as dazzling in the regular theater. The opening sequence of Joker's cohorts crossing the buildings and Batman's decent off of Sears' tower are both obvious, but exhilarating. And not just those scenes, there are lots of "Oh wow!" moments (the 18 wheeler/bazooka sequence), as the action is balanced perfectly along with the plot, for if either had dominated the other, the full impact of the film would've been less than completely satisfying. Even with all the trite material that floats around the box office today, it's nice to see a film made that's not afraid to give its audience a nice, swift kick - something they're not ready for, something they might not be able to handle - and then watch to see how they cope with it.

Little more can be said... The Dark Knight was simply brilliant. Never have I seen a comic book movie explore the metaphysical depths of morality, bad conscience, resentment, vigilantism, and justice to the extent that Nolan does here. The story takes so many abrupt left turns and on-a-dime twist that it leaves you as dizzy as the breathtaking action sequences are themselves.If there were any flawed traces left in those tautly edited reels they are erased by mesmerizing performances from the entire cast. Freeman and Caine's chops ranged well beyond just being two clever and witty old men. Bale surpassed what he did for Begins. Eckhart is able to take a somewhat clichéd character (thematically and in appearance) and generate it into someone complex, brooding, and yet seemingly fragile.Ledger's performance alone should and will haunt you for years to come. He truly becomes what he proclaims himself to be, and agent of chaos, a juggernaut that fuels anarchy and tragedy like an all consuming fire. Despite how disturbing and unnerving his humor becomes, you can not help but give a macabre chuckle. The sequence where the Joker appears in a nurse's dress becoming frustrated with an explosives detonator while bangs and fire surround him is a riot.Believe the hype! This is may be one of the best movies of the year, let alone the best movie of its kind.

Review Title: The Movie grabs you by the neck, and you will like it
Review: It always happens with movies, before one is released, we have sneak peeks, trailers, posters and more that invoke interest for the fans and non fans alike. The anticipation reaches fever pitch and we moviegoers become so hungry for the movie in its totality that our hunger can only be shunned by watching it. But sometimes, the expectations from a movie are so high that even if it is good, truly good, we still think in our minds that it could have been better, we find something missing. And then there are movies like The Dark Knight. I had seen Batman Begins and thought, Christopher Nolan had single handedly picked a comic book superhero from under the dusty shelf, cleaned him up and put him right up where he would be thoroughly appreciated. So my expectations for The Dark Knight, after watching the trailers were more, than usual. I was a hungry wolf, one that hadn't eaten warm flesh for a long, really long time. But after sitting through 152 min of TDK, I was stuck for words. Here is a movie that caught be by the neck, didn't let me move or breathe and it felt good. Nolan's latest had surpassed all of my expectations, not by a few miles but by light years. Right from the first scene with the camera swooping in on the jokers in trademark Nolan style, with brilliant engaging background score by Hans Zimmers, to the gripping climax, my brain cells were constantly being overwhelmed as my heart forgot to beat let alone maintain its rhythm. Heath Ledger as the Joker trounced some of the best performance by the great actors of today and yesteryears. This is what acting is all about, Heath made the audience feel for him instead the Batman. He injected that lethal dose of madness on to every person watching the movie, including me and left us thinking. Jack Nicholson, you were good, but sorry, really, Heath is truly what the Joker is all about --- an unimaginable personification of madness, lunacy, and fearlessness, a character that cannot be charted. Heath's performance was so gripping that, his character felt like the main lead instead of the Batman himself. Christian Bale nevertheless did a great job again as the caped crusader. I won't talk about the other characters because, I am still unable to think beyond Heath Ledger's performance and Nolan's flawless direction. More importantly I need to catch the next show, and watch the movie for the third time since its release. Just go watch TDK, it truly is a masterpiece in every sense of the word. Watch it for its mind-numbing stellar direction. Watch it for its great performances by each of the perfectly defined characters. Watch it for its brilliant background score. Watch it even if you aren't a Batman fan. But most importantly watch it for Heath's performance as the Jokerwhy so serious?

It isn't an overstatement to call The Dark Knight the most sophisticated and ambitious work of its kind. Superior to all three Spider-Man installments and even its amazing predecessor in terms of conceptualization, writing, acting, and direction, Nolan's follow-up to Batman Begins is a dark, complex and disturbing film, not the least of which because it grafts its heroics onto the blueprint of actual reality rather than that of spandex-clad supermen. The Dark Knight Review: The Dark Knight is the movie of the century. Rather he created plots that would be shot best in 2D with the touch of IMAX. With the perfectly coordinated stunts shot at various angles gives more life to the story. As this movie is the second installment in the Batman franchise, the story is continued from the first part 'Batman Begins'. David Goyer and Nolan brothers have done a tremendous job with the story-telling. The screenplay of the movie is so absolute that from the very start of the movie it gains interest. Another best thing is cast of the movie. Senior actors like Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman joining high potential actors like Christian Bale, Heath Ledger in this so called superhero movie is treat to watch. Every actor has played its part perfectly. Starting from Ledger, he has given his best performance till date. The Joker portrayed by him gives full view of the character physically and mentally, making him best villain so far. He was so much into character that he did his make-up and 'Joker videos' in the film by himself. Actor like Michael Caine forgot his lines after watching him in a scene shared by both of them. He totally deserved Oscars which he got posthumously. Bale, who portrayed Batman in all three parts seemed more comfortable in suite than in Batman Begins. He played billionaire Bruce Wayne like he is one. Giving perfect expressions of caped crusader has made him Best Bruce Wayne played till now. Screen shared by him and Ledger made the movie what it is. His love life Rachel Dawes played by Maggie Gyllenhaal has given justice to the role. She has indeed showed the love for Bruce Wayne in a darker way perfectly. Their intense and darker love story supported by Aaron Eckhart (Harvey Dent) gave the movie a heart touching experience. Michael Caine played the role of Bruce Wayne's butler so well that everybody wants a butler (or father) like him. His advice to Bruce Wayne from his own experiences in various services made Batman wiser and clearer of his vision. No one could have played the role of Lucius Fox better than Morgan Freeman as it was written by keeping only him in mind. He is so professional that he knows which toys Batman will need for his purpose. Also taunting him (Bruce Wayne) about life showed his soft corner towards Wayne. Gary Oldman who normally has negative roles in all his movies has played role of Gotham's finest police very well. His incorruptible character justified his actions in the movie and Batman's faith on him. Aaron Eckhart (Harvey Dent) did very good job first playing positive and then negative role. It seemed like he actually doesn't know the inside story of the Batman. Remaining actors mainly policemen with Gordon and Mob bosses gave their 100% in the movie. Cillian Murphy (scarecrow) also did very good job with his uncredited scene. The dialogs of the movie were epic and very refreshing. Especially Joker's laughter. Dialogues delivered by Ledger perfectly suits the character and tells why he deserved an Academy (Oscar). No one can beat him for that role. The stunts performed maintained status of Nolan and the name of the movie. The movies actually has many genres including crime, drama, action, mystery, superhero, thriller, romance (in darker way) etc. Music is given by Hans Zimmer. No explanation is needed further. His background score itself gives feel of intensity carried throughout the movie. After watching this movie you will get to know why this movie is recommended by so many and why it is best superhero movie. This movie is so good that if you watch this movie for 1000 times still you will be as excited as you were for the first time. This movie was released in 2008. Many big movies have released after 2008 still this movie has stayed in top 10 of IMDb's top 250. Watch this movie if you want Larger than Life experience and breath-taking performances in World class Cinema. Review Title: Wow. Seriously, What a great film.
Review: Heath Ledger was amazing. Just flat out, insanely brilliantly. His turn as the joker is sure to be remembered as one of the most in depth and startling interpretations of any villain, comic book or otherwise. When you watch him, you aren't watching Heath Ledger, you're watching The Joker, and you can't watch anything else while he's on screen. His mannerisms and facial expressions express his insanity so well, and it makes him all the creepier. The Joker in this movie is truly disturbing, as his motives for his crimes is not money, rather just to watch people suffer. Ledger does an incredible job bringing a new and more intense Joker to life. I honestly feel that Heath will win a posthumous Oscar, not just because he died, but because he DESERVES it. Not many actors could pull off what he did, and he should be recognized for it.As for the other actors, they all did a tremendous job, and I feel sorry for Aaron Eckhart, as his character does not get much attention even though he as well acted his part beautifully. Christian Bale is, as always, a fine actor turning in a fine performance. It seems that whenever Christopher Nolan and Bale team up that they produce a film that is nothing short of a masterpiece (The Prestige). Michael Caine as Alfred delivers some charming comic relief which is quite needed as this film is quite dark. I was surprised by how psychological it was and how the main struggle in this movie was a moral one. I was expecting far more explosions and action sequences, but the dialogue and emotional turmoil was just as satisfying.I know people are saying that this film does not live up to the hype and that this movie's success if fueled by Ledgers untimely death, but I just can't see how thats true. The acting, the music, the cinematography and, most importantly, the directing all garner 4 stars from me, and this movie deserves all the praise that has been heaped on it, at least for me. Congratulations, Nolan, you delivered a hell of a film. Can't wait for the third.10/10.

The Dark Knight (2008)Christopher Nolan again blows our minds away with stunning effects, great writing, and a phenomenal cast of the most talented actors and actresses in the movie business, when he brings back Christian Bale, as Bruce Wayne, his alter-ego Batman in The Dark Knight (2008) as well as Michael Caine, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman. Some new faces are, Heath Ledger and Aaron Eckhart. There really is no better way to describe The Dark Knight (2008) than as the "Holy Grail" of all movies. The sequel to Batman Begins (2005), The Dark Knight has broken records of all sorts, such as becoming the second movie of all time to break 500 million in the Box Office, and also having the biggest weekend's total, out of any other movie made. The Dark knight brings back Christian Bale as Gotham City's billionaire man, the owner of Wayne Enterprises, Bruce Wayne. Faced with all new problems and a new villain in the mix of thugs Batman must now deal with The Joker (Ledger). Batman (Bale), Lt. Gordon (Oldman) and new District Attorney Harvey Dent (Ekhart), set out to take out the remaining crime bosses and their pawns completely from Gotham City. While trying to put the rest of them behind bars, a new criminal mastermind sets foot in Gotham and sets out to take over. The Joker gets on a personal level with Batman, forcing him to think about what really is most important in his life.Heath Ledger took the role of the Joker, and showed why he was the right choice for the part. This being Heath Ledger's last full movie with a main role, he definitely did not disappoint. As Batman tries to build his symbol as a hero and protector of Gotham City goons are out to destroy it and take back the city they once had. Trying to decide whether or not, being Batman is what he really wants, Bruce Wayne is also faced with the dilemma of keeping his relationship with Rachel Dawes close to him. Aaron Eckhart, plays Harvey Dent Gotham's District Attorney is also trying to fight crime and build a symbol for him while trying to avoid being assassinated and keeping a relationship with Rachel Dawes. Christopher Nolan displays Batman's power and importance by choosing to shoot a broad range of close up and low shots. Nolan also does this with Ledger's character the Joke. The Dark Knight is a movie of great darkness and that is why most of the movie's scenes are shot in dark, very dim lighted ways to make the movie have that eerie, scary feeling. Nolan shows in great detail the massive chaos and special effects, with ingenious camera shots and lighting. This movie is great for teens and adults with its riveting screenplay, brief romance and intriguing plot. Being rated PG-13, some parts and images could be too intense for some young children. Any Batman lover or comic book enthusiast will greatly appreciate all the Christopher Nolan put into this movie. Rating this movie with five stars, it should be seen by everyone. Nolan is able to make it seem as if the viewer is right there going along with every punch, kick, and explosion that The Dark Knight has to offer.

What we fail to realise is that during our youth we were subject to a style of film that allowed us to mature into it, there isn't one person alive that can tell me honestly that the first time we saw star wars, we understood everything that occurred, we knew what 'the Force' was or even that we saw coming the twists that intertwined before our very eyes. What we were subject to was cinematic history in the making, just like the way we did when we first experienced bullet time in the Matrix and the concurrent disappointment that transpired with the dire and subsequent franchise. What we see with Batman is that happening again. I cannot say in good conscience that Christian Bale is my favourite Batman because he is not. But what I can say is that he is the lead character in my favourite film. Despite the merits that Heath Ledger has as a psychotic and realistic Joker we do not experience the apathy with him that Nicholson brought. The love of a fiend, the understanding of his plight. We do however empathise with his family as they suffered his premature death. Keaton will always be the Batman and Nicholson will always be the Joker but what we have is a movie that will never die and a series of characters that are permitted to develop in a way that the first star wars enthused us to believeit is a wonderful film. A dark film. A film that says to us as comic book and film lovers, this is how it should be

The new Batman series, made by Christopher Nolan, may be considered a true consequence of the contemporary tendency of rationalizing the imaginary. We are trying to find a reasonable and scientific explication for all the fantastic elements with whom we meet. In the first episode of the new series, Batman begins, we see a Batman who could very easily exist in your own town, with a perfect plausible explication for everything, suit, vehicle, mantle and so on. As an obvious continuation, in The dark knight the battlefield is extended to a larger area witch includes Honk Kong, a more palpable location. But the feeling of a fantastic novel is returned by the character named Joker. The whole line of events revolves around this character, a man with no identity, no personal history and no actual explication of his deeds. Only his line explains: This town deserves a better class of criminals. The good vs. evil battle is not very well shaped in the first episode, where an almost moralizing character, Ra's Al Ghul, whose destiny is connected with the mysterious organization, The league of shadows, does not succeed in creating a veritable negative character. His goal, destroying the evil, purifying the world, is not a brutal or sadistic purpose, it is born out of a tragic past. All this changes in The dark knight with the help of the Joker who shows the true essence of comics, the battle between good and evil, with both sides very well shaped so that the audience would not be confused about the identity of sides. The defeat of the negative character gets more important after Christopher Nolan gives the simple citizen a different role other than a simple observer, a simple victim. He is now an active element of the story , well emphasized in the boat scene, a true suspense moment. The connection between Batman and the population he saves in everyone of his adventures is stronger than ever in The dark night. The joker is defeated but not terminated, leaving a reasonable reason for the story to go on. Christopher Nolan's production becomes an outstanding episode in the cinematographic representations of Batman, a real proof of contemporary cinema. We can say that this is the most intense continuation of the first episodes, true expressionistic manifestations signed by Tim Burton.

Review Title: Batman seen in the visionary light of Christopher Nolan. A kolossal full of action and evil philosophy
Review: Christopher Nolan is the director of complex movies that need to be watched and understand in their deep meaning. They are, somehow, "interpretable" in different ways. And so is this film. It is not the usual superhero movie where the good fights against the bad in epic battles. Action scenes are alternated with proper "moral" fights. The Joker is one of the few evil men who proposes to the audience his own philosophy. This valuable characteristic distinguishes him from the other villains in the film, who seem to have no personality (they are in fact portrayed in a weak way, and his attitude towards the world involves both the citizens of Gotham and the audience. Joker manages to transform a honest man (Harvey Dent) in a vindictive villain. Nothing in the movie is no-sense and the words that come out from the mouth of the characters are well-chosen (and they are often taken repeatedly). Naturally, action and suspance scenes are present and they are extremely well-shot. You can enjoy the film in all its parts because they are balanced so as not bore the viewer.

Give him the Academy Award and any other awards that he could possibly qualify for.

Review Title: The way a Batman movie should be made!
Review: The Dark Knight is easily the best Batman movie to date. Christopher Nolan clearly shows the darker aspect of the Batman comic and how much more realistic it can be.Even if you do not like Batman or superhero movies in general, one reason to see this movie is Heath Ledger. He not only steals the show but his character will be remembered forever (clearly should be nominated for Oscar). His take on the Joker is brilliant so much that you forget during the movie that it is actually Heath Ledger. Christian Bale seals the deal with Batman yet again (except for an annoying overdone deep voice). Gary Oldman puts an even better effort then the previous one and Aaron Eckhart does a good job exploring the world of Two-Face.The movie lives up to its expectations and beyond and sets a bar for any future superhero movies (or any movie for that matter) for years to come. The Dark Knight has everything you could want in a movie: action, great acting, drama, love story, twists, humor and of course Batman.Do not listen to anyone who tells you this is a bad movie because that is plain stupidness. You don't have to like it, but you have to respect the greatness of this movie!10/10

Review Title: We finally meet the real hero.
Review: Reviewing this movie is very difficult because I could go by my emotions or praising its artwork. It also seems pointless because with so many reviews and almost everyone already seeing it I wonder if anyone will read what I write. Still, there may be that one person. If it's you...Go! Now!! Yes, Heath Ledger was spectacular. What you need to know, however, was that he not only was a terrifying joker, but he had a little bit of that comical insanity that Jack Nicholson brought to the screen in 1989. So, he may haunt you, but he will also make you laugh...and laugh out loud.The character of Harvey Dent is the one that few people have said much of, and I find him to be the more important of the two. Yes, the Joker was the real nemesis, and Ledger probably did the better performance (and though I don't see an award in sight, a nomination does seem worthy). However, the story would not have been what it was without the character of Two-Face. And Aaron Eckhart had a wonderful way of making that character the danger that he was and still remain the Harvey Dent that we cared about.In my opinion, most importantly, the real surprise for me came from no longer watching this film as though I was looking to find out what happened to Batman, how he began, or even how he would protect his identity. In the end this was the first "Batman" movie where I was actually waiting to see what Bruce Wayne was going to chose. As you have probably heard if you've read many reviews this is not written as a comic book movie this is a crime saga with the characters of a comic book. This became an epic tragedy where we finally got to know the hero that we have been following in the theater for nearly 20 years.In the end, this felt different from any fun book I've read, epic novel I completed, film I watched, or flick I enjoyed. I want to put it high in my all time favorite list, but it's hard to find anything to compare it to. All I can say is that even if this is not one of the greatest movies of all time it could easily become a legend.

Review Title: Best yet comic book to big screen adaptation....period
Review: Christopher Nolan's "The Dark Knight" is by far the best and most suspenseful Batman adaptation made to date. Throughout the movie I constantly forgot I was watching a comic book movie and felt more like i was watching a mixture of Clockwork orange(1971) and Heat (1995). This is an intense thriller which offers a stellar cast with the exception of Maggie "toadfish" Gyllenhaal who is more suited to a dry comedy under the direction of maybe Wes Anderson. She does however do the role well, but I am used to hot leading women in Bat flicks, it feels like watching a James Bond movie with Julliette Lewis or Christina Ricci acting alongside Sean Connery or Daniel Craig, the thought just frightens me frankly. The performance of an all star lineup including Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon is A grade as is Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman, however my hat goes off to Aaron Eckhart (Thank you for Smoking) as the white knight District Attorney who plays the role brilliantly especially his transformation into Two Face, which is played out so well both in acting and in script writing. There are so many twists and turns throughout the film which keep you constantly engaged that I didn't even realize it went for 2.5 hrs, but it could have gone for 4 and I would have soaked up every minute just as much. Bale's acting as Batman is always amazing as is expected but Heath Ledger as the murderous and anarchy laced Joker is the backbone of the entire film. His performance makes Jack Nicholson look like a gay sailor period! The story which revolves around the Gotham Mafia hiring the Joker to seek and destroy the Bat by causing chaos by threatening to kill public officials very day unless Batman reveals his true identity which pans out with so many twists I felt like I was watching Nolan's Memento (2000) and makes the film cinematic genius. This ladies and gentlemen, Jews and Gentiles....is how a comic book should be made on the big screen and the public would agree as the movie broke records for biggest opening weekend EVER ($155.34 Million) clearing Tobey Magiures Spider-Fag 3 off the top listing. I recommend all to see this feature as it is truly an epic film. Lastly, on a darker and more touchy note, Heath Ledger should not win an Oscar for this role. Knowing Hollywood's sentimentality's the award will probably be given to Ledger for reasons beyond his acting performance. Whether he is dead or alive should have nothing to do with it . But hey remember that Denzel did win an Oscar for Training Day (2001) when Sean Penn had to bite his tongue after his superb acting in I am Sam (2001). Overall this is an instant classic and is in my top 20!

Review Title: Going crazy waiting to talk to someone about this movie!
Review: OK, I went into this movie expecting it to be great, just like some of the other films I've seen this summer were great. But it wasn't great. It was so POWERFUL that I've been going online for the last two days reading reviews on it because no one else I know has seen it and I have to share this experience somehow. It was so dark and disturbing without being "Seven" that I find myself haunted by some of the things that happened in the film. When I saw it at the noon showing on Friday, the pact theater kind of chuckled at some of Heath Ledger's early lines and actions. Soon, like REAL soon, the entire theater was got DEAD QUIET every time he was on screen. And it wasn't because they were bored, because I was quiet too, like he was THAT intense! Don't get me wrong, Aaran Eckhart was just as good as Heath was but he wasn't creeping me out most of the time. If anything, he made me feel safe, even more than Batman did. I wanted to vote for him, for ANY office. I believed in Harvey Dent. I keep wanting to hold onto Michael Keaton as my favorite Batman. But I can't anymore. Christian Bale found himself surrounded by incredible actors, hidden behind a mask half the time and he still managed to keep from getting buried. This was a Batman film. I keep seeing reviews where people complain about Christian Bale's voice as Batman but I liked it because it made sense (as did everything else in this movie). It gives him a sense of instability that he needs if he's going to try to intimidate people who aren't easily intimidated. Not to mention, it keeps people from figuring out he's Bruce Wayne. I think comic book movies are okay, but they always feel like comic book movies, like the hero will save the day and probably by some improbable act. This didn't feel like that. Everything in this movie seemed frighteningly real. Like REAL! A lot of the reviews I read say this is the best comic book movie ever. But I say it's a sweep at the Academy Awards. Now if only some of my friends would hurry up and see it!

Review Title: Wow. This films is... Just... Phenomenal. Best film I have ever seen.
Review: The Dark Knight.The Dark Knight is a film which follows on from Batman Begins, the origins of Batman, and that was a brilliant film. But The Dark Knight completely exceeds its prequel. It is an absolute masterpiece, the ensemble in this exceptional crime, thriller, action, drama, is one of the best I have ever seen.Christopher Nolan, in my opinion, is the best director ever, the way he creates an atmosphere is astounding. I love the way he has taken 'Batman' and turned it from being stupid and quirky into something brilliant. The darkness really brings out how great Batman and the other characters are. And the actors who betray them do it brilliantly, Heath Ledger especially. Christian Bale did just as good at being Bruce Wayne/Batman as he did in 'Batman Begins'. But then they introduced the Joker, and Heath Ledger was selected to play this crazy, schizophrenic maniac. And he did it better than anyone has/could of. Jack Nicholson, step aside, Heath Ledger brings this character alive and makes him truly unbelievably brilliant.The story of this film is incredibly thought out, very clever and fully enjoyable. The screenplay was incredible, I never thought I could get so into a film, but I couldn't take my eyes off of my TV screen. The ending of this film is the best ending to any film I have ever seen. It is so action packed! Everything just comes together, and there is not one boring moment. The sound to this film meets the standards to the video completely, it doubles the excitement.This film is not to be missed whether you like Batman/superhero movies or not. It is a brilliant film for people who love excitement and tension. Buy this film and watch it. In my opinion, this is the best movie ever made.

Review Title: Excellent Film- Better Joker than Batman
Review: I have never really been a Batman fan. I like the 60's series with Adam West, but I've never been particularly drawn to the story, especially not in other mediums. So, why, when I saw the trailer for the Dark Knight, did I instantly want to go see it? I'm not quite sure, myself. I think it was the eerie darkness portrayed in the trailers, the dramatic music. Or maybe it was the Joker. Obviously, due to Heath Ledger's untimely death, the film has been receiving enormous buzz. One can only assume that, had he lived, the film would have been celebrated, but not as "big" (think Ironman's buzz). Sadly, of course, we will never know.The plot can be easily found on this page, so I won't go into detail. All I will say is that Gotham (a dark and nearly unrecognizable Chicago) is under attack from the mob and,of course, the Joker. Batman is not being regarded as a hero, more as a vigilante, and the citizens are crying for him to turn himself in.Christian Bale as the Batman was passable. I have never been a particularly big fan of his, and his deadpan throughout the movie did not stir up any emotion in me. I found myself not caring much about his character- never a good thing. Maggie Gyllenhaal, Gary Oldman and Aaron Eckhart were all good at their respective roles in the film. But, of course, everyone I've heard from is talking about Heath Ledger as the Joker.And he is superb. His voice, his laugh, his character's little quirks (licking the jagged scars around his lips), all make Heath Ledger melt away and the Joker emerge. I felt somewhat the same way as I did the first time I saw Edward Scissorhands- Johnny Depp became the character, and he as an actor was practically invisible. You saw only Edward. The same holds true for Heath Ledger-- you see only the Joker, except for the one time his greasepaint was taken off; he was shown only for the most fleeting of moments, but I practically did a double-take: "Heath Ledger??" I heard a film critic say that the Joker did not appear to be having fun. I watched the film and can say that it looked to me that he was. He laughed maniacally at the things that made others cringe and he appeared to really enjoy being supremely evil. This film was very good, and I whole-heartedly recommend it to anyone that had any interest in it. Even if you only go to see the Joker, that is reason enough. He is the reason that I have rated it 9/10, not the Batman.

I've never been much of a batman fan, but I watched this movie because of the good reviews. What can I say? I really didn't like it.Action scenes - no idea if they are meant to look retro or if they are just badly filmed. They didn't bring up any tension at all. I didn't feel in the movie but just left out.Story - as lame and predictable as a superhero movie story can be.I could just go on and on: superficial dialogs, bad costume and make-up (Joker), mediocre sound-track ... and - oh my god - the voices of both Batman and the Joker. I just waited for Batman to say "Luc, I am your father ..." with his voice modulator ...After half of the 153 minutes I fell asleep (I really did), and that had never happened to me in an action movie. I continued the next day and hoped that at least the second half would get a little better. But no. No good story, no climax, bad action scenes if any; repeating scenes in different locations with slightly different dialogs ...Sorry, but what are the good ratings for? It isn't a completely bad movie and I might have given 5 stars if not for the expectations after reading through other reviews. But it is far away from 9 stars.

Although being a sequel to ''Batman Begins'', ''The Dark Knight'' does not in any way rely on it's strength.This film stands proudly on its own. A true gem in the history of films that from beginning to end shows us an epic struggle of life...I can safely say that each scene in this film is brilliant in it's own right.It violently grips you in the exceptionally outstanding opening to leaving you with a wild frenzy of emotions in the last...Christopher Nolan directs one of the best casts and maybe the finest line up of characters we will see in a long,long time. But Heath Ledger as The Joker is always the surrounding hype of ''The Dark Knight''. Be that as it may,his performance as The Joker is light years away from what makes this such a unique masterpiece.I'm not saying I didn't like his performance. I think it's one of the best portrayals of a character captured on film that can be compared to even praised Brando performances. The Joker performance is one of the many elements that makes the film exceptional. It's the entire cast and their ability to act out against each other. Christian Bale,Heath Ledger,Aaron Eckhart,Gary Oldman,Michael Cain and Morgan Freeman...Take a bow.The score.The darkness of the score creates an ''out of this universe'' feel to the film which compliments it's realistic tone. It really is another major element in this amazing film.I can't talk about the story without giving spoilers, but as I said, it's a beautifully orchestrated masterpiece.All in all, The Dark Knight has majestic timing with all of its amazing elements coming into being at the right moments. It has really been an amazing feature to have witnessed this rare piece of art...A brilliant story crafted with creative theatrics...It is because of films like this the art of cinema came into being....

Review Title: Not as good as the hype
Review: Other comments have listed the inconsistencies in the plot line so I won't repeat them. This was a good film but really, needed some light and shade! By about 1 hr 40 I'd had enough and just wanted it to end - there is such a thing as too much action/gloom/desperation and the really best films realise this and lighten the mix with humour. The acting was good and I especially enjoyed Michael Caine and Gary Oldman - Heath Ledger was riveting in his performance and all the more scary as there was no other reason for his actions than to cause pain and chaos. A bit like some of the terrorists out there today! There were some really moving and scary bits - Maggie Gyllenhall's end and when Gary Oldman's family are being held - you could feel the fear of his children - Heath Ledger as the nurse was stunning but it didn't add up to a 'great film'.For the UK, this film is given a 12A rating but there is no way I would take a twelve year old to see this. It should have been given a 15.

Review Title: It is by far, the best portrayal of the Joker to date.
Review: This was an astonishing and ultimately the best comic-book film made, and even made the best comic-book villain portrayed by a great actor who played his character well and live in our hearts forever."The Dark Knight" was well composed, sequences amazing, and the story was magnificent. So many reasons as to why Heath Ledger made the Joker the way he was and made him so perfect are ways that no person - I believe - will ever be able to beat.Having so much enthusiasm for the role, by locking himself up for 6 weeks to come up with the menacing voice and terrifying laugh that he created, absorbing the mental stability of a psychopathic schizophrenic with acute PTSD, no one can match his dedication (even though rumoring about Heath taking meds to make the character seem more twitchy - I believe - was not the case or one of the reasons he made the Joker his best role). Heath is the reason how the Joker and the film one of the greatest films of all time.

Review Title: A great Batman movie, that's all

Review Title: Good God, this movie is amazing!
Review: This is by far the greatest movie I have ever seen. Christopher Nolan reached new heights, and created a masterpiece. Let me start with the acting. Heath Ledger is one of the most underrated actors ever. He fit the role of the Joker much better than his previous actor, Jack Nicholson. Every word he said was more insane than the word before it. His list of famous quotes stretches more than 100 yards long. He is scary, mischievous, and downright psychotic. His crazy schemes almost always come together, and they they push their victims to the limits. Christian Bale also performed extremely well, but not as well as Ledger. He was a great Bruce Wayne, and his part was terrifically written. Aaron Eckhart and Gary Oldman also performed extremely well, and their characters helped make the movie what it is: amazing. The suspense in this movie pushes you to the edge of your patience, and when it finally pays off, oh boy is it good! I can barely find anything wrong with this movie. It is nearly flawless.

Review Title: Probably the best action film of all time.
Review: You may have begun watching this movie with already high expectations after the excellent "Batman Begins", but I promise you, this film surpasses them.This is, in many ways, is the culmination of Nolan's impressive Batman trilogy, and it profits extremely from one of the greatest performances ever put to screen by Heath Ledger as the infamous Joker.The film is a wild ride, you will not feel bored at any point. Review Title: The Dark Knight - The Climax of Comic Book Movies.
Review: The Dark Knight is rather hard for me to put into words. Sublime, Superb, Fantastic, Amazing, Incredible, and Unbelievable don't give it justice. This movie flows with such ease you don't even know where the two hours and thirty minutes went. Yet I fear that this is the climax to all comic book movies, from here on they will never be this good.I'll start with the one who brought this movie together, the glue, and that of course is the late Heath Ledger. His performance was spectacular better then I could have imagined. His portrayal of the Joker in his twitches, movements, speech patterns, and actions in general are exactly as how I saw the Joker. I didn't see acting when I watched Heath as the Joker, I saw a completely different person, he fully immersed himself into that role and played it flawless. I am a HUGE movie guy, and his performance was better then what I have seen in many of the films today. I can't describe it, you feel his presence and you believe in his character to be a true person. Heath made this movie into the masterpiece it was with this performance, and at the least deserves a Oscar nomination for his role. If Johnny Depp, was able to gain a nomination for Jack Sparrow Heath should have the nomination for best supporting actor sealed. It's just winning the Oscar, which will prove to be the hardest goal due to the comic based film and all the movies set-backs towards the academy.Nolan, the director and co-writer, made this film feel like a rollarcoaster ride into hell. Yet, in the best way. The i-max scenes are amazing in sound, size, and spectacle. The robbery scenes bring back memories of the movie Heat or Point Break, yet adds a new touch to this old concepts to Bank Robbery. He and his brother, John, wrote this script is written to perfection, due to the plot points it makes by using the characters to drive the plot, especially Harvey Dent and the Joker.Bale and Aaron Eckhart played great roles, yet I do think Aaron out did Christan acting wise in this movie. Due to the many layers that Dent has in his character. He brings Dent alive and the Two-Face character to an even greater extreme. Bale did well, but was rather out-done by most of the cast in this film. He still did play the role of the playboy billionaire to perfection.This movie is not just a popcorn flick, it can be seen as way more. it proves some very solid points on order, corruption, and sanity. It makes you really think about how you would handle yourself in the position the characters are in. This movie has my pick for movie of the year, hands down. And not just comic book movies, I mean all the movies that have come out.

Having grown up watching Bill Dozier's TV homage to the comic book hero, maybe I went into this with an unfair expectation of the principal villain in TDK. I wasn't looking for the howling Cesar Romero necessarily, but there was nothing even remotely wry about this film's Joker. Are we to believe this character is named the Joker simply because of the angle of his facial scars? I guess that might be enough for some, but I wanted the Joker to wield a devilish sense of humor as part of his arsenal of terror. Heath Ledger delivers a terrific psychopath, but a Joker he's not.Relationships seemed amiss in TDK. Where was the genuine if frequently sarcastic warmth shared between Alfred and Bruce in Batman Begins? Did anyone really believe there was much passion between Rachel and Bruce in this version, despite a much better performance from Gyllenhaal than Holmes? Even the wonderful Morgan Freeman had little to do in TDK, other than monitor the preposterous-even-by-comic-book-cinema-standards wall of cell phone data from what... 30-million Gothamites? Yeah. That could work. Lt./Commish Gordon's interplay with Batman misses the mark as well, and I felt the Gordon family anguish was forced.I've read some unflattering comments about Bale's performance. For me, he wasn't given much material with which to work. In Batman Begins, his character has far more dynamic range. TDK further quashes Bale's work by over-graveling his Batman voice to the point that only constipated anger can be effectively emoted.At least Eckhart and Gyllenhaal were given some latitude to develop their characters, though I never fully surrendered my heart to their oft-stated love.Complaints aside, for theater thrills TDK brings it home... outstanding production design, great effects, superb sound, and another great collaborative effort between JNH and Zimmer on the soundtrack.

Review Title: Not the second coming, but still a great movie
Review: Everyone has been acting like this is the greatest movie ever made or something. I thought it was good- I had a great time watching it, and appreciated the whole attempt to be deeper than a comic book film thing. I didn't think it was the second coming of Christ or anything though. I'm sure I am in the minority, and people will react like they do when you say that you thought Apocalypse Now was overrated and bloated, or that Quinten Tarantino sucks, for the most part.Anyway, I'd say this is the best Batman movie yet. Christian Bale still has that horrible voice when he's Batman, and still does the whole Patrick Bateman/American Psycho thing when he's Bruce Wayne. Heath Ledger's Joker sounds like Andy Dick or something. And here was my biggest problem. This was a good performance, but it was NOT a groundbreaking performance by any means. I think when posthumous actors have roles like this, people tend to over-blow it- kind of like they did with Brandon Lee in the Crow (another good performance, but not a performance for the ages, by any means).I can appreciate the whole Zen/Anarchy/pseudo Fight Club philosophy stuff Ledger was going for, but he's no Frank Langella as Skeletor. I mean, it's definitely better than the whole Jack Nicholson paradigm, but he still just came off like a wannabe Tyler Durden/Bodhi from Point Break with schizophrenia. The real star of this movie is Aaron Eckhart, who is great as Harvey Dent/Two Face. The cinematography and plot twists were really something to behold, and I applaud the filmmakers for continuing the standards set in 'Batman Begins' and not turning the Dark Knight into another mindless, popcorn munching summer blockbuster. The only really negative thing I can say about this film is that, for a film that takes itself so seriously, and clearly expects to be measured against truly great cinema, it just falls a little short. Not the second coming, but still a fun, "thought- provoking" (AHEM) movie. Score another one for Christopher Nolan and Goyer.

Review Title: No disappointment here, ladies and gentlemen
Review: It was difficult enduring month upon month of media frenzy concerning "The Dark Knight" and Heath Ledger's performance. Was it Oscar-worthy? Is The Dark Knight the greatest superhero movie of all time? Is it worth paying 7-ish bucks to go see? Yes!The Dark Knight follows the path of its predecessor, "Batman Begins". Christopher Nolan reunites with Welsh actor Christian Bale in continuing the clean slate that lifted the hopes of so many Batman fans around the world. The movie is set not long after the last; Bruce Wayne/Batman (Bale) is as unsure as ever as to what his duties to Gotham involve and what he represents. The Joker (Ledger) has come to fruition about what needs to be done to prevent Gotham from being completely cleansed in deciding to "kill the batman". Lieutenant-Commissioner Jim Gordan (Oldman) faces the challenge of keeping the Batman and the Joker in check all while keeping a weather eye on his own shifty department. District Attorney Harvey Dent (Eckhart) faces almost the same as Gordon, with a little more love-triangles and politics thrown in there. Rachel Dawes is involved with that love triangle, and last but certainly not least, Lucius Fox needs to keep Batman's secrets and provide the cool stuff.Now to the part that everyone really wants to hear about. The acting. It is superb, to say the least. I dare to compare the performances to that of legendary movies "The Godfather" and "Pulp Fiction". Christian Bale does the job as well as he did in Batman Begins, having more on his plate this time around with showing that 'darker' side of Batman. Heath Ledger does what everyone was talking about - he brings a "psychopathic, schizophrenic, mass-murdering" clown to life in a way that no other could possibly do. It was stunning. The Joker stole every scene he was involved in. The amount of change undergone from a witty Nicholson to a bone-chilling Ledger is unnerving. Everything from the terrifying cackle to the gangly posture - Ledger certainly brought his A-game here. Hannibal Lecter has a replacement as the most frightening villain in film. Anything less than a posthumous Oscar wouldn't be fair.Fantastic performances go all the way through to supporting actors in Gary Oldman and Aaron Eckhart. Oldman does a fantastic job in personifying a stressed out Commissioner who's mind is juggling on three different fronts at once. Eckhart, I will admit, surprised me. I was a little uneasy when I heard of his casting, but I'm glad the doubt was proved to be out of place. He finely portrays Harvey Dent's masculinity and fire as a District Attorney. Maggie Gyllenhaal puts Katie Holmes to shame with the amount of depth portrayed upon a near-flat performance from Holmes. And of course Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman do what they do best in playing the guiding, authoritative voices in Batman's background that leads him through the tough times. I can honestly say I was not disappointed with one performance throughout the entire movie.The cinematography and special effects are Oscar-worthy. Chrisopher Nolan succeeded in preventing The Dark Knight from becoming a over-zealousness of CGI and explosions, and the city of Chicago never looked so dark and gloomy to me before. Well done.One thing I would never mention in any other movie, but the music in this movie was top-notch. I'm not talking a random alternative song thrown into the background of a car chase, but a superlative composition that makes the darker moments darker, and the colder moments colder.In the end it seems only fair to commend the genius hiding behind the curtains: Christopher Nolan. The man has not only rebooted a quickly dying series, but he has done it in such a way that there is no turning away from the pending sequel. The depth that he has injected into the characters. The direction of the film. The technical quality overall. Truly amazing. I'd get into all the details concerning the theme of morality and the brilliant message that the ending provided, but I don't want to ruin it for any potential viewers. I was scared the movie wouldn't be able to find a proper ending for itself, that it would be like so many other lax endings to superhero movies, but the ending capped off a true masterpiece that had the entire theater in a standing ovation. Christopher Nolan along with his writing staff have created a masterpiece of the filming industry, one that can only fairly be called the greatest superhero movie of all time; arguably even bigger than that. Step aside Spielberg, your CGI mish-mash is outclassed here.In 152 minutes you get a hero born, a hero that's doubted, and a psychopath that wants them both dead, all amongst twists and turns that are enough to plunge one into a feeling of euphoria that will last a lifetime.

Review Title: To Date, The Best Film I've Ever Seen
Review: A huge fan of the Batman movies, I have been excited since the end of Batman Begins. Picturing how the Joker would be portrayed in a film directed by Christopher Nolan flat out excited me from that last scene. When Warner Bros. announced that the Joker would be played by Heath Ledger, I thought, "Heath Ledger, the guy from the cowboy movie?" I had never seen Ledger in any films before, and definitely could not see him pulling off the Joker. I mean, come on. The Joker is crazy, insane, morose, I could go on all day. Honestly, I could not see Ledger doing anything near what I expected from Nolan. Boy, was I wrong...My friends and I had been scrambling for tickets to see The Dark Knight at the ever popular midnight showing. However, (quite embarrassingly so) none of us could drive past the PA Junior License Curfew of 11:00 PM. We thought to take the bus, go with older friends, or sheepishly ask one of our parents to come along with us. I was scared I wouldn't see it opening weekend. But what are sisters for? My sister, an intern for NBC10, had told me about a month ago that she had entered a contest to win tickets to the July 17th Philadelphia premiere of the Dark Knight. "A long shot," I recall telling her. Though she did not win the tickets, her boss had plenty of extra tickets, which he was not reluctant to give away to employees. My sister nabbed 2 tickets, each with one guest permitted. Sorry to my friends, but how many times does this happen to someone? I was nervous at first, asking people I work with what its like to see a movie on IMAX. "Can you see the whole picture?" "Am I going to be looking up the whole time?" Needless to say, I could see everything, and my neck was nice and comfortable in the bucket chairs at the Franklin Institute. Enough about my experience, let's talk about the movie.I had already declared (without seeing it) the Dark Knight to be my favorite movie of the summer, and quite possibly the best Batman film to date. My heart was pounding in the opening minutes as a result of the overwhelmingly large screen and the excellent camera work, but it settled down throughout the two hours and thirty-two minutes. As the movie went on, I thought to myself, "This is incredible." Christian Bale has already won my vote for the best Batman since seeing his stellar performance in Batman Begins. He did not disappoint in his second showing. Charming and witty as Bruce Wayne or heroic and physical as Batman? Bale proved he can do both, and both well. Although his performance is undeniably spectacular, he does not earn the Best Performance for this film. That, my friends, would go to the late, absolutely great Mr. Heath Ledger.As stated before, I did not see Heath Ledger as someone who could do wonders to Batman's undisputed rival. Seeing him in trailers and pictures before seeing the movie itself restored faith in Christopher Nolan. However, neither the trailers nor pictures did justice to the performance Ledger gave in the Dark Knight. His voice, his makeup, his general being on screen simply blew me away. Being able to transform himself from a character such as Brokeback Mountain's Ennis Del Mar to a corrupt, evil character such as the Joker truly showed me how versatile the man was. Now, as I had mentioned earlier, I have never seen any of his films before. The Dark Knight was probably the best way to introduce myself to Heath Ledger. This may upset whoever is kind enough to read my review, but I would like people to know what I am about to say. Quite honestly, since the day I heard Heath Ledger has passed, I hadn't really cared. But how could I be if I had never seen any of his films and knew so little about him? Thanks to his performance in the Dark Knight, I now care not only about the actor he was but also the person he was. My hat is off to you, Heath Ledger; may you rest in peace. The Dark Knight is truly magnificent. As I'm sure anyone who has visited the IMDb page for the Dark Knight has already seen it, I recommend it to anyone and everyone. I honestly could not see how anyone could dislike this film. It is by far the best film I have ever seen, and so far, the highlight of my summer.1 million/10Jordan

Review Title: the dark knight - About how several minds get together against one no mind
Review: Sir Caine and Mr. Freeman for most part did not manage to do anything better than the begins. I liked Aaron Eckhart in parts. The new Rachel Dawes was definitely better than the previous one but nothing spectacular. Batman - is helplessly loosing confidence. Bruce tries his best to do something about what is going on - But was more confident in the "Begins". (May be he is aging or loosing his spirit over time) - Joker is portrayed as a mindless dark humored being bringing batman to his knees.. Joker's acting is alright and well contained with no complaints. Nolan continues his mind games he started with Memento. His "begins" presented us an installment of mental weakness - how Bruce fights it.. Here Bruce is shown giving in to a mindless brute who is mindfully playing the cards. So what makes Dark Knight that special - Well The Heath Ledger Surprise - He blew every one before he blew himself and proved Brokeback was not a flash in the pan. His portrayal of Nolan's take on Joker came as a complete surprise. And that alone sets the mood. A menace that is simply going out of control. "Even" batman has to give in. I still think it was Nolan's take - But Ledger gave his own identity to it. Spectacular performance - I cannot comprehend. (Again only because I did not expect it from a guy like Ledger. ) Though Nolan tried his best to choke you with emotions - I still think the movie was a little lengthy - But do not know where to chop. Music - photography and everything else was in place. (Take the joker's performance out - and there is little to the movie) I heard people comparing Ledger with Mr. Nicholson - I wonder why Jack did not think in these lines - Do not know how much artistic freedom he had at that time.. nevertheless - I liked Heath's portrayal. As much as I liked Dan in Casino Royale. Good Job Nolan - pulling off another successful Batman installment. Let batman be a man - use his mind to play his opponents in the next installment. Sometimes it gets hard giving in is not a solution.

Review Title: The term 'masterpiece' isn't good enough for this film...
Review: I myself have always been a fan of Batman-I saw the first film in theaters with my parents when I was three (which may have been too young and DEFINITELY is for The Dark Knight), and I was hooked ever since. With this mindset I automatically assumed my biased opinion of the character would take control of my real thoughts on The Dark Knight film. Well. It definitely didn't hurt, but I think I would have loved this movie even if I had never heard of Batman going in. So far I've seen it five times and am going for a sixth tomorrow--in fact I can already say it is my favorite film--I don't even want to think about the movie that actually holds a candle to The Dark Knight, because I don't think anything as flawless as this film is going to come along for a long time.A few movies I would compare it to would be the first two Godfathers, Heat (Chris Nolan even has a reference to Heat i.e. William Fictner makes an appearance), and possibly--as far as the crime is concerned as well as the ceaseless care taken with the script. Chris and his brother Jonathon pay the utmost attention to detail--so much so that I have yet to see the movie and not notice something new each time. Everything from the soundtrack to the cinematography--the costumes and wardrobes to the set designs were as close to flawless as I have seen. That being said, I know roughly ten or fifteen people who are NOT Batman fans--and a few of which who do not even generally like this type of film say they LOVED it...and justifiably so as it is SO much more than just a Batman movie, or just a comic movie, for that matter.As for the acting...well it's all been said before, but even so I have no choice but to say it as well: the acting was superb. Heath Ledger has already received about as much--if not more praise for his portrayal of The Joker, as Javier Bardiem did for No Country For Old Men. In my mind, there is no performance that will even come close in terms of focus, commitment, and overall presence. I pity the actors who go up against Mr. Ledger WHEN he receives an Oscar nomination.Christian Bale, Gary Oldman, Michael Caine, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Morgan Freeman...all of these performers brought so much depth to the film and made it into one of the best ensemble casts I've seen since Pulp Fiction. Each of said mentioned names fell right back into character and delivered remarkable performances, save for Maggie Gyllenhaal who is a newcomer to Nolan's Batman series. She did something that surprised me: she took her role of Rachel Dawes in a completely different direction than Katie Holmes. While most people bash Katie for her portray of Rachel Dawes, I didn't have a problem with it. Sure, I would say it was the weakest link in Begins, but it still did not bother me. Maggie Gyllenhaal on the other hand pulled off a very difficult feat. She managed to remain the tough, independent, assistant D.A. that the role called for with absolutely no compromise while simultaneously pulling off something her predecessor did not: she had very good chemistry with Christian Bale. In addition to that, she also had great chemistry with Aaron Eckhart.To conclude, the movie is a 'masterpiece,' but even that word doesn't seem to do enough justice to what Christopher Nolan accomplished which is the most ambitious film I've seen in a very long time. My only regret is that we can never see Heath Ledger reprise what was hands down his finest performance. It remains ironic to me that his finest performance was synonymous with his darkest hour. His death was untimely, unfair, and in my firm belief nothing more than a stupid mistake with the worst kind of consequence. My condolences go out to his beautiful little girl. Hopefully, when she's older, she'll watch this movie and appreciate what her father had to go through in order to become what he did on screen. With a little luck, she may learn what he gave to become The Joker--a role that will NEVER be topped and never be forgotten...and a role that I am forever grateful Heath Ledeger chose to accept. I also hope one day Matilda Ledger will see the staggering amount of people who watched her father play a character (and loved his performance as much as I did) that could easily have turned into an imitation of Mr. Nicholson's own performance--and understand that he put everything he had into it. I hope she will understand what that kind of passion took to energetically, and consistently portray his character, and what the cost was.Heath Ledger, took the Joker and instead, of imitating and merely updating the role, he took it in a completely new direction (aided with Chris Nolan's screenplay) and created the most masterful performance I have ever seen--one that I doubt will ever be topped (at least in my eyes), by anyone. Thank you for sharing your passion with the rest of world, Heath. You will be missed, but never forgotten.--Jason
