Review Title: Christopher Nolan please take a bow
Review: The Dark KnightYes i have watched it four times and still have not got enough of this movie.The first time, i was so awestruck to even notice anything other than the grandeur and the sinister mood of the movie. The second time i went to watch it for the chase sequence where the Joker is chasing Harvey Dent. It kept on lingering in my mind after the first watch. The scene where the Joker sticks out his head of the police car sums up the perfection of this movie.The third time, what hit me hard was the characterization of every single person. I think a good movie is the one which makes you go through the same feeling as depicted on the screen.Here we have a gamut of them , chaos,guilt,endurance,sacrifice,faith...in other words a complete exhibition of human emotions and how they face the test of dilemma when such conditions arise. This movie gives you both cerebral and visceral quality. The agent here being Joker. It is really sad that we will not be able to see Heath Ledger in any other movie but i thank god that i was lucky enough to see his masterpiece. "either you die a hero or you live long enough to see yourself become a villain"--A tribute to Heath Ledger.I cringed for Harvey dent, felt sorry for him, i laughed at the sinister jokes and felt guilty of having done so, I could feel the dilemma of our beloved Batman, and at the end could feel a sigh of relief and resignation to the fact that he is not a hero, he is much more than that.Each and every character undergoes a change (morally, physically) under the chaos created by Joker (the best depiction of a psychotic Joker -- who at times is a child but a grown up person who likes to fiddle). The greatest fiddler in the history of cinema. Even the disappointment, bewilderment and guilt in the face of Rachel,when she comes to know of Bruce Wayne's decision, has been beautifully captured. Music is awesome. It gets your heart pumping and racing even if the story does not (which is not possible here). Gotham city looks very much in chaos and the dark sets enhance the dark mood of the movie. Cinematography is excellent. Dialogues have been very carefully written (Jonathan Nolan seems to keep on churning thought provoking dialogs in each and every movie).Especially the monologue that the joker gives to Harvey dent is amazing. "i am like a dog chasing cars, i would not know what to do with it once i caught it"Lastly Christopher Nolan had you not been the director, this movie would have failed to live up to the expectation after Batman Begins or even surpass it. To tell you the truth i am being unfair to the beauty of this movie by selecting a few scenes to drive home the point. You will have to see it in order to feel the anarchy , the chaos and the thirst for more of this movie.

Review Title: Why so sad? I'll tell you why...
Review: Heath Ledger creates a brilliant character and you can't wait for his appearance back on screen. Some of the scenes (like the one from the police car or the one where he's dressed like a nurse) are absolutely beautiful. Apart from that, there's a big nothing. Christian Bale didn't seem to be trying too hard. As great as he is, useless philosophy dialogues can't be acted, especially when the "dilemmas" are identical to the ones in the first series. The excessive hoarseness transforms him from obscure and mysterious into tired and sad. When you see him flying and killing/saving five people at a time, but then about to die in an encounter with a rottweiler, you suddenly understand why the poor bastard lost the will to live. Maggie Gyllenhaal is one of the ugliest women i've ever seen on the big screen. You'd swear she is the reincarnation of the mummy from "tales from the crypt". If they had put all the males in the movie fall in love with a boot, it would have brought a lot more credibility and a much greater emotional impact on the audience than this.The look of a senile old broad who always seems cramped because her morning enema hasn't kicked in yet transforms all the romantic scenes and the emotional preoccupations of the young female lawyer into an uglypeople.com experience. The rest of the actors are mediocre, or just plain awful. But you have nothing to demand from them with such a script. The difference between The Dark Knight and other mainstream super-hero B movies is that instead of one bad movie, you get two, stuffed together, two and a half hours which could have easily been one and a quarter. It's a lot for the mere asking. And I'm not just talking about the so exaggerated action scenes : the huge truck that tips over because of a cable, the helicopter that falls down because of another cable, the bazooka fired from a 3 m distance, and last, but not least the overwhelming scene with Batman taking down 50 men using ropes and hooks, while gazing with white eyes around him in the building. Nor am I forgetting Morgan Freeman who can listen to 30 million telephone conversations in real time, destroying the entire system after he finishes because he can't bear the thought that it's "immoral". Even when you see Two-Face looking worse than the 90's version of The Terminator, you still think maybe something good is going to turn up in this movie. Although all this makes you want to leave the hall, these aren't the biggest problems of the film, because you're willing to accept the the Hollywood spirit "we spend 'till we don't have anything left" if the story stands on its own two feet. But the story seems to be crawling like a wounded animal, and the fact that it's two and a half hours long makes the agony seem to last forever. Your eyes hurt when you see all the nursery philosophies about justice and morality, supported by the stories of wise Alfred about Cesar and the outlaws of Birmany. You get tisks in your spleen when you see the woman-cop with the hospitalized mother, the martyr prisoners or the emblematic blond child who's about to die, but doesn't die and at the end thinks that Batman is good. When you realize that every ten minutes you'll be surprised by another twist in the story you start feeling a slight internal bleeding. And when you see that the witty plans of blowing up Gotham are still at the level of the well known 80's cartoons you can't handle the pressure anymore and the blood starts gushing out through your nose. At the end you can't help but wondering just how stoned the writers were when they came up with all thin nonsense and why you decided to waste your money on the ticket when you could have spent it on something better. Overall, the movie is neither dark, nor gritty, not even psychological. It's a great Heath Ledger, a hoarse Bale, a horrifying Maggie and a brass band of bad guys so well packed in a jar of pickles, that not even a fibster could breath. A movie sold thanks to an extraordinary man, who didn't live to see his outstanding performance. Unfortunately, the rest of the Hollywood stars, writers, producers and promoters didn't move at all. They probably just laughed their brains out when they saw the huge rate that this movie got on IMDb.

Review Title: this isn't a Movie, it is a Life
Review: FYI: The following is my very first movie review. After watching the trilogy for 100 (literally) times (that was kind of a vow), I finally decided to write a review on it. The very first thing I noticed the first time I watched it was "NONE", I couldn't understand a word of it because my English was so bad and the picture was so blurry (that might seem awkward but the DVD I got at that time wasn't original. It was actually filmed illegally in a movie theater, by the way that is quite usual in my country!). Two years later, I was a changed man. I became familiar with the IMDb and developed a particular interest in movies in myself. In my journey through the "Top 250" list I gave "the Dark Knight" another try (this time the DVD was genuine), AND IT WAS UNBELIEVABLE! The movie I never respected was actually the best (again, literally) movie I have ever seen! First of all, there was technically very little CGI and that is absolutely respectable and special for a superhero movie. Secondly, it really demonstrated the very nature, soul and idea before all the superheroes: "sometimes truth isn't good enough, sometimes people deserve more, sometimes they deserve to have their faith rewarded". We cannot live on our own, we need and we deserve "mythical superiors" to help us. Sometimes the truth is too unbearable that we have no other choice but to replace it, misinterpret it with a "myth", a "lie". The myth could be "A GOD", "GODS" or even heroes: imaginary but inspiring. After all (not to offend the ones who believe) the God (or gods) is also made by the imagination of the Man, although the passing of time might make us to think that they are "real" but they are not. It is also noteworthy to understand the magnitude and the immortality of an "idea" and the trilogy represents this concept perfectly, just like V for Vendetta. Last but not least, it does not help to pretend that you are strong, and it might even bring horrible harm to you. If the reality is too dark, you just need to open the door and go "outside".

its the best batman ever. I had the honor of watching The Dark Night during a screening and was completely blown away! Many of us movie-lovers watch a lot of movies. Some times, it turns out to be a disappointing experience. Most of the time, we like the movie, but forget it after a few days. However, there are those rare moments when you watch what is called a masterpiece, and it sticks in your mind for your entire life. This review is about one of these. This review is about Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight.The Dark Knight is the sequel of the very good Batman Begins, the first movie of The Dark Knight trilogy. It is a masterpiece because I think it will change how movies in general will be made in the future.Its dark and claustrophobic tone fits perfectly to a Batman movie. The Dark Knight shows that the tone of a movie influences the viewers experience. Throughout the entire movie, we feel that the main character is not totally in control, that it's an all new and different challenge for him and that he doesn't know how to handle it. And that brings me to talk about the Joker. Of course everybody knows the Joker, how he looks, how he is, etc. We even know how he acts because of the great performance Jack Nicholson pulled in Tim Burton's Batman. Actually, everybody had that performance in mind when they started the movie and that is also the reason why Heath Ledger's performance is so astounding. He brings the character to an all new level and in a completely different direction, but still in a very believable and accurate way (in my own opinion, he nailed the character even more then Nicholson did). Ledger made the Joker so crazy but so right about everything at the same time. Even if he is a psychopath, we understand his motives. It is so sad that Ledger died before the film's release and that he couldn't see all the impact his performance had on the film industry (personnaly the greatest performance I have ever seen by an actor). Gary Oldman, Aaron Eckhart, Christian Bale, Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine and Maggie Gyllenhaal also all gave incredible performances. The plot of the movie is also very interesting and refreshing, leaving behind the classic three acts structure. The score of the movie, composed by James Newton Howard and Hans Zimmer, is perfect, very good and very appropriate. The movie itself also looks very good and has a great cinematography. Nolan directed this movie in the best way possibly imaginable.To conclude, the movie is possibly one of the greatest I have ever seen if not the greatest because of the mind-blowing acting, the great score and the perfect directing. The movie is also great looking. It's the perfect batman movie, with it's most iconic villain and, in my own opinion, couldn't be better.

Review Title: The Dark Knight - The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly (no spoilers)
Review: Just finished watching it and I have a lot of mixed feelings. Please not that the only issues I have with the film are stated here. Other than what I write here, I think the film was excellent.The Good: It took half the movie to convince me that Ledger's performance as The Joker was as good as everyone said it was. I am not swayed by hype nor am I by intense special effects. To me a movie has to do more than just LOOK good to BE good. I admit I watched Ledger's performance critically. I had to to keep the tragedy of his death from making me be biased by pity towards his performance. For the first part of the film he seemed a little one-dimensional. He was just a common, crazy loon with a gun and that was all. No other levels. But then, as his plot unfolded, Ledger raised the stakes just a little bit at a time. Like subtle ticks of a clock. He added more colors. There was an emotional palette behind The Joker that had depth and substance. Now I don't know if this was direction of if the actor's choice to hold back for so long. Either way it was risky. VERY risky. He took a chance that I doubt I would have had the guts to take. By the end of the film, with The Joker in full blossom, I saw the man for what he truly is.Pure evil.Thank you, Mr. Ledger. You have just raised the bar on what good acting is.Almost everyone in the film turned in a fine performance. Incredible characterizations all around with solid, real choices. If there were an Oscar for Best Casting Director, this movie would win it.The special effects were spectacular and frankly I can't remember when I have heard a better script. The lines were, for the most part, well delivered and the pacing was as perfect as I have ever seen in a movie.The Bad: Not a big fan of the look of Gotham City. I was spoiled by Burton's vision. He put the Goth in Gotham. It was dark. It was an oppressive organism that sucked the soul out of its citizens. One look and you said, "Well geez! No WONDER crime is rampant there!" This new Gotham is just too...normal. It looks like every other major city and I miss the darkness that Batman both embraces and fights against.The Ugly: I hate Christian Bale as Batman. There, I've said it. It took me two movies to figure out WHY I don't like Batman Begins. As spoiled billionaire Bruce Wayne, he is excellent. He has charm, charisma, a boyish, impish gleam in his eyes. As serious Bruce Wayne, the man who went on a crusade to bring justice to Gotham, he is strong. He is defiant in the face of corruption. He has a determination that is unquestionable and undeniable. As Batman I can't stand him and it's all because of his acting. Because the actor's face is hidden, I can't take into account facial expressions. Because he is hidden in shadows and wears a large cape, I can't see his body language. All I have to judge his acting as Batman by is his voice - the way he delivers his lines. He is a flat, Johnny Two-note. He is either Batman trying to be scary (and sounding ridiculously comical in the process) or he is Batman trying to sound mysterious (which he actually does occasionally pull off). Every time he spoke as angry Batman, I either laughed because he sounded funny and delivered his lines poorly or cringed because he just totally ruined a brilliantly intense dialog with another character. I think I would love Christian Bale as Batman if someone else dubbed his lines. I could give you specifics of the lines I thought were brilliant and the ones I thought were horrible, but I promised no spoilers.All in all, TDK was a great movie with, for the most part, performances that now re-define the face of acting. Was it "The Greatest Superhero Movie EVER" as I have heard so many say? No. Is it a worthy contender for a tie with such films as Superman: The Movie, Superman II, Batman (the original with Keaton and Nicholson), and Iron Man? Definitely.After all, take away the special effects, the incredible stunts, the lavish sets, and fantastic costumes, all you have left is two things: Story and performance. You can have the greatest story and the strongest script but, to quote Khoury's Immutable Laws of Theatre, "One good performer cannot save a bad show but one bad performer can ruin a good show." Bale's performance as Batman is the sole issue that kept me from loving this movie as much as I wanted to. I think when I get the DVD, I'll just mute him every time Batman speaks while angry. That way I can savor his performance as Bruce Wayne AND Batman.

Besides being a top-notch superhero flick, The Dark Knight is a gripping thriller that surely raises the benchmark for future superhero movies. For a film with a running time of 152 minutes, it is amazing that The Dark Knight does not have any dull moments. The fast-paced tone of the film is set from the first scene itself. Director Christopher Nolan goes into much darker territory with this film that is reminiscent of the critically acclaimed 1980s graphic novels The Killing Joke and Dark Knight Returns.After his hard-hitting performance in Batman Begins(2005), Christian Bale proves yet again why he is the best on-screen Bruce Wayne/Batman. Throughout the film, he comfortably switches between the goofy playboy Bruce Wayne and the gruff-voiced vigilante Batman. Batman's struggle with ridding Gotham City of all crime continues in this film and it is made more difficult by the rise of a deranged killer called Joker.At last, two of Batman's most formidable nemeses  Joker and Two-Face  are portrayed in a manner that is true to the comics. Even before the film was released, there was much hype over the late Heath Ledger's performance. After seeing this film, I truly believe he deserves every bit of accolade. He brings out the real madness of the Joker, being both funny as well as scary at the same time. Compared to Jack Nicholson's Joker in the Batman(1989), his portrayal is more sadistic and maniacal. Then there is Aaron Eckhart, a highly underrated actor, playing Harvey 'Two-Face' Dent. Eckhart fits into the roles of the virtuous Harvey Dent and the vengeful Two-Face with such ease that you can't help but marvel at his acting genius. Like a lot of comic book fans, I hated Tommy Lee Jones' campy take as Two-Face in Batman Forever(1995). Thankfully, Eckhart's performance helps in erasing those painful memories of Batman Forever.Veterans Morgan Freeman, Michael Cane and Gary Oldman return to their roles and make for a strong supporting cast. Special mention should be given to Maggie Gyllenhaal in a very heart-warming role as Rachel Dawes.Apart from these superb performances by the actors, the visual and sound effects are breathtaking. The script is very tight with no loopholes and the editing is really crisp. Techno fans will love the new Batsuit, Batpod and array of gadgets that Batman uses. Special kudos to the cinematographer for the awesome camera angles and lighting techniques. All in all, it is a high-octane entertainer that delivers what it promises.

Review Title: The Greatest Superhero Movie ever made. Period.
Review: Batman has always been my favourite comic book hero, and watching The Dark Knight makes me overwhelmed that Nolan has truly done justice himself to the Caped Crusader.With all the summer superheroes films leading up to this one; such as Iron Man and Incredible Hulk, The Dark Knight delivers a quality feature film, that at points in the film you forget is even a Superhero flick. With outstanding performances from an All-Star cast, The Dark Knight has single handedly schooled all Superhero films ever created. I felt at the beginning that I was going to be impressed but with the Introduction alone I was blown away, Nolan keeps the film very experimental in ways, almost getting right to the point rather than these derogotory title sequences that we often have to sit through at the beginning of a Superhero film. He creates tension and gives you a slight thriller aspect to the film, causing you to feel very anxious and at times even petrified about what is taking place.I have never really been a big fan of Heath Ledger, I have enjoyed him in films, however when I read a year and a half ago that he was to play the Joker I must admit I was disappointed, However, after seeing him portray the Joker in such a twisted and psychotic manner, I can truly say that he owns that role. Michael Caine, once again portrays and outstanding performance as Alfred as Bale does of Bruce Wayne, however Aaron Eckhart was also outstanding, an really does shine throughout this film, often stealing the spotlight from Bale, as Ledger does.Nolan kept the film as a film, and didn't sell out for a strain to make the film 'child-friendly' which often you look around the theater and think to yourself, 'are these kids allowed to watch this?' The film is very grown up, and feels just as fresh and original as Begins, exactly what a re-boost of a franchise should be. Also the fact that he wrote alongside his brother just goes to show he had the vision for where the film should go, way before they even switched a camera on.The action and suspense is also not solely caused by the Heroes and Villains but is also surprisingly caused by the situations, and even the pedestrians, or those with lesser roles. Gary Oldman, also really delivers as Gordon.Where do I end? I simply can't. In simple terms, GO AND SEE THIS FILM, and if you have already, then see it again, and again, and one more time. Christopher Nolan hats off to you. You have brought us what will be the Greatest film of 2008, and the greatest Comic book adaption Superhero movie of all time.

Review Title: Ledger Gives a Legendary Performance in a Great Film
Review: Not being fan of comic books or movies adapted from comic books, I remember going to the theater with my friends thinking I wouldn't care for The Dark Knight, after it ended, I'll admit it wasn't bad, but it wasn't great like everyone was saying it was. Then after some time passed, I watched it again, and I was blown away.Heath Ledger, who in most cases is THE reason the film became so loved, gave us an academy award winning performance that was undoubtedly the best of his tragically cut short career as Batman's nemesis, The Joker. In fact, Ledger actually locked himself in his hotel room for a month and kept a journal during filming to become engulfed with the character, and for most of the film it doesn't look like he is even acting, he IS The Joker. It was the best portrayal of a villain in a film since Sir Anthony Hopkins' legendary role of Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs, and I personally believe Ledger's Joker is second only to Hopkins' Lecter in terms of being scary, creepy, but also very interesting at the same time.As great as Ledger is the film, there actually are some other great performances. Gary Oldman is more than respectable as Gordon, Aaron Eckart as Harvey Dent is, to me, the second best role in the film, and Christian Bale does not disappoint as Bruce Wayne/Batman.Technically, the film is also very well done. An academy award victory in sound editing and nominations in cinematography, art direction, film editing, and visual effects prove that film passes all aspects of the eye test with flying colors.The Dark Knight is one of the best films since 2000, in my opinion. The #4 spot on the IMDb top 250 also doesn't hurt. It is a must-watch for not just Batman fans, but any fan of great films.

the answer to the question, ' does it live up to hype?' is definitely No. it is infinitely better than the hype and is spectacular. the dark knight is film-making at its very best. be it action, performances, intensity, effects, direction, screenplay...its got it all. and it would be correct to say that people who don't watch it are missing out on cinema at its zenith i honestly though memento was Nolan's best work (not ignoring prestige or batman begins) but fortunately i was proved wrong. his direction is immaculate...i really have no words to describe it. it is truly his tour De force and one only hopes he keeps giving us this kind of cinema. the movie explores the fight between good n evil to higher limits...whether it is correct to give in wen there is so much loss or whether to endure them? it treads finely between good n evil n shows us the line is very very thin. Christian Bale as batman is solid...he comes out on top to probably a more difficult role than the prequel...this time the conflict within him deepens and he portrays it with a very mature performance doing complete justice to the idea that he is the best actor to have donned the bat-suit. Aaron Eckhart proves his mettle as an actor with the transition from a confused yet strong crusader to a deeply distressed villain: two-face. the change is very real and smoothly done. his talent was never in doubt...it was the consistency...it is a performance to be truly applauded. Gary Oldman as Gordon is fantastic and the depth to his role from the prequel has made him come out with splendid acting. Gyllenhall is good as Rachel but the only thing not convincing with her is her looks. she looks too old for a woman who both dent n batman wanna die for. Caine plays the role of Alfred very well n looks like a true guardian of Bruce Wayne. Freeman is convincing as well...but isn't he always... n now we come, to probably one of the best performances in decades...the best acting i have seen so far. Heath Ledger as joker makes Nicholson's portrayal look bad (it was before this considered very well done). Ledger completely transforms into the joker n puts his heart n soul into a role that will never be forgotten. be it his demonic laughter or his intense n sometimes emotional summarization of a psychotic person. there is not one second in the movie where u feel its ledger...u believe he is the joker. he brings a chill to your spine every time he enters a scene. it is his finest hour...alas also his last. i mourn the loss of such an amazing talent... summing it up...the movie is what legends are made up of...it ranks up there with the godfather, pulp fiction... a 10/10

Christopher Nolan's second bundle of joy "The Dark Knight" EXCEEDED all of my expectations!!! With the success of 2005's reboot of the Batman franchise, they took what was already established and expanded it, amped it up, and gave a deeper, darker and brooding story that is more gripping and the suspense is likely to catch you of guard several times throughout. Christian Bale delves more deeper into Batman, sworn to fight evil and injustice, though also quite reluctant and uncertain if his crusade can ever end and cleanse his inner turmoil from his fractured soul due to the murder of his beloved parents. But with the help of his trusted butler/ally Alfred (played superbly by Michael Cane) grounds him, gives him moral support, and keeps him in check. But the real star of the show is Heath Ledger as Batman's most deadly enemy, The Joker. I can HONESTLY tell you that: as good as Jack Nicholson was in Batman'89 he is CHILD'S PLAY compared to this Joker. He is sadistic, psychotic, and downright SCARIER and PSYCHOLOGICALLY disturbing than the previous incarnation of The Clown Prince of Crime and Ledger gives it his all to do him justice. Along with the original cast comes some fresh faces such as Aaron Eckhart, Maggie Gyllenhaal and more. I must say though I liked Katie Holmes, Gyllenhaal gives a much better performance and is a far cry from the "damsel-in-distress" stereotype (though there's a little of it, THANKFULLY) that's common in films. Bale and Gyllenhall have MUCH better chemistry this time around more so than Holmes. Even better, the fight sequences are vastly improved and feature more brutal and bone crushing combat than "Begins" in addition to new technology at Batman's disposal. Also worth mentioning is screenwriter Jonathan Nolan, who gives the film an added frosting to an already delicious cake. Simply put, The Dark Knight is totally more bad ass than "Begins." The action is great, and the plot is more deeper and engrossing. I applaud Christopher Nolan, Christian Bale, and especially Heath Ledger (who sadly passed away earlier this year) and all those aboard for believing in Mr. Nolan's talents for this second installment. Although some may feel a bit of melancholy over Ledger's death, but as a final note I will say this sincerely from my heart: Remember Heath Ledger and honor him in your minds and hearts not only for his performances, but as a human being and father to his daughter Matilda Ledger. May we issue him best wishes for his family and friends and his daughter for years to come.

Review Title: The Greatest Superhero Movie of All Time
Review: Batman: The Dark Knight is the greatest superhero movie of all time. Its cinematography, pacing, and acting are unmatched by any other movie of the genre. However, it is also one of the greatest movies ever created. It is a masterpiece in its craft. The portrayal of The Joker by Heath Ledger is outstanding and he deserved the Oscar he received posthumously for the role. The tension and the set pieces are amazing. Nolan's use of practical effects is what makes the movie so visually appealing, unlike a movie such as Avengers: Age of Ultron with the massive use of CGI. Bale's second portrayal as the caped crusader is one that puts him down as one of the greatest Batmans of all time. Harvey Dent's transformation is also done with perfect pacing as the audience slowly see the character's attitude and morale change throughout the movie up until his transformation from the explosion. Also, the editing is done so intricately and perfectly to a point where the viewer never wants to look away from the screen. This movie is a MUST SEE!

What can I say about the Dark Knight that hasn't already been said? I've watched it around a dozen times (twice in the theaters) yet I can find nearly no flaws in it. It's simply fantastic.Some people allude the popularity of the film to the success of Heath Ledger as the homicidal and menacing Joker. But Dark Knight is much more than that. Dark Knight is a realistic, dark take to Batman's fight against crime. In the film, Batman continues his crusade to save Gotham from itself and inspire hope, and is making great progress. The civilians are stepping to the streets themselves, the new District Attorney Harvey Dent is admired by many, the police have reformed themselves and criminals don't dare go out at night. That's when Batman's polar opposite, the Joker steps up, bringing chaos, anarchy and raw dehumanization where ever he goes. As Batman struggles to keep the streets safe and the criminals locked up, the Joker just wants to lower everybody down to his level, to embrace the violence and madness. The film is about the grey areas between the heroes and the villains. How do we stop a man with no rules nor boundaries while clinging to ours? How far can we go to enforce justice? Gordon, Dent and Batman all have to make decisions to protect Gotham, but also to protect it's humanity. The heart of Gotham, finally starting to believe in good again, is threatened when it's greatest protectors are forced to make impossible decisions. Instead of the straightforward fight against what's clearly evil, they have to ask themselves what is truly important.The Dark Knight is a philosophical, complex and intelligent movie about humanity and ideals. A film that spawned a dozen quotes and catchphrases, it makes you think and marvel. It's sophisticated, intense and enjoyable to the core, from the setting to the score to the themes and to the acting. The Dark Knight is a meaningful superhero film and a modern classic. It set the bar up for movies everywhere, and I doubt we'll see one like it again.

I just got out of an advanced screening for The Dark Knight. You may be asking yourself: but Gutterball, it's Monday and everyone knows that this movie opened on the last Friday. To that I say: with a movie of this prestige getting to see it on a SOLD OUT Monday night is an advanced screening. So, the biggest movie of the summer could be the biggest movie of the year? Well with the attention that this movie has been receiving since Heath Ledger's untimely passing one can't be terribly surprised. But did it really live up to the hype? Was it better than the very remarkable as the first installment? Yes, and yes. The Dark Knight was everything I thought it would be, and so much more. Christian Bale is Batman, this movie cemented that for me. He was the main character, but he certainly wasn't the main attraction. I don't know if you heard, but Heath Ledger is playing the Joker in this one and all too soon people are screaming for an Oscar nod. Well, I will say that Heath Ledger was remarkable. I will even admit that sleeping may prove difficult tonight, but the highly coveted Oscar for Best Supporting Actor seems, even with such a strong performance, just out of reach. You see, Ledger was a powerful actor. See: Brokeback Mountain or Candy. But at the end of the day, when Christian takes off that mask, and Ledger takes off that scary make-up it's still JUST a Batman movie. Let me show you what I mean. Could you imagine if this movie came out last year and Ledger's untimely passing happened last year? Picture an Oscar nod with last year's contenders. You had movies like Into the Wild and Michael Clayton. Could you see BATMAN up there too? I know I couldn't. It's still just a superhero movie and if Leger does get the nod I don't think he really deserves it. It was a good role, not to put the role down. But it WASN'T Oscar worthy. That being said I'll get back to the actual film. I am a big fan of dramas. Action movies never appealed to me because I think that there must be something wrong with someone who pays 10 dollars to see people beat the tar out of each other for two hours. But a film that can entertain with tar-beating and actual story line is a rare combo, especially in a superhero movie. Spider-Man was able to do it, but when Spider-Man 3 was released I think we all forgot about how good the series was and how bad it is. Batman Begins was a super movie, but it was only one. Now we can say that Batman is a DC series, and with the installation of Dark Knight it is, in my not so humble opinion, the best superhero series out in the last five or even ten years. Let's just hope that despite Nolan's hesitancy we haven't seen the end of Christian Bale donned in black.

Review Title: One of the best movies ever
Review: This is one of the best movies I have ever seen. I left the theater speechless. I enjoy - and expected - a typical comic book movie and, with all of the hype, was ready for a let down. This movie is dark and deep and violent and is nothing like any comic book movie ever made...I forgot that it even was a comic book movie. I don't even know how top describe it. It is a combination horror/thriller/detective/psychological/action movies. It shows how fine the line between good and evil can be. The Joker will go down as on the the finest psycho characters in film history, alongside the likes of Norman Bates and Hannibal Lecter; it was the performance of a lifetime (no pun intended). On a negative note, the movie didn't "flow" very well; it did seem a bit choppy in parts and was a little long. The movie doesn't completely absorb you. That probably has something to do with "editing", one of those film credits no one usually pays attention to. Maybe it needed a better editing. Regardless, this movie is a must-see.

However, he did an unbelievable job. Even with all the hype about his character, during most of the movie I forgot it was even him behind the makeup. When you are able to focus more on the character and not the actor (especially in this case) you know he's doing an awesome job.Maggie delivered a much better performance than Katie (not trying to hate on her, though). I believe all the actors did an incredible job.There was a lot going on and it was indeed a very long movie. But honestly, the time flew by. With all of the twists and new people popping up, it certainly kept my attention.I'm no crazy person and I realize most of the events in the movie aren't going to happen. But I loved how for a "superhero movie" or whatever you would like to call it, it was more realistic. No offense to Spiderman, but he wasn't flying from building to building on a spiderweb. It was more technology than actual "super powers" and I loved that.I'm not like some of the other people who walked out of the theater shouting about how super sweet it was, or recapping on some of the amazing parts. Ledger not only brought the comic book to life, but also expanded on the characters by creating little mannerisms.Aaron Eckhart plays Harvey Dent. Eckhart portrays Harvey as a man who is trying to clean up the streets of Gotham.Michael Caine and Morgan Freeman reprise their roles as Alfred Pennyworth and Lucius Fox. Both actors continue to build off from where their characters left off from Batman Begins.Maggie Gyllenhaal plays Rachel in this movie. Review: I saw The Dark Knight at the IMAX. The first shot, as the camera zooms over the city scape and the whole audience gasped. The amazing visual effects, towering eight storeys around you, wowed us all as we set off on the roller-coaster ride through Gotham's darkest times.That gasp from the audience really wasn't the last gasp either. The IMAX enhanced effects, Heath Ledger's JOKE, some pretty stunning direction and all round good acting made this one of the best productions I've ever seen. But when I saw this clinch the number one spot at IMDb, I worried for it.No one could expect a DC Comics film not be American through and through. However, even the most hardened comic fan couldn't help but wince at the references to terrorism, the blatant advocacy of invading the privacy of citizens and torturing prisoners (though only when necessary, of course), and the amazing idea that the people will unite, through democracy, to defeat the evil that is chaos and replace it with the good that is conformity.The corny lines are, generally, within the acceptable limit (you need some in a Batman film for goodness sake) and a plot would stand up to a fair amount of scrutiny, something few comic book films deliver. That said, the film constantly seems to be ending, then a new twist takes in forward. When it does end, we suffer the monologue summary that now seems compulsory in any blockbuster, presumably so that the increasing number of effect-seeking media-illiterates can still understand what the point of the past two hours was.if, however, these comments are starting to give you a negative vibe, please stop reading. This film is good and should be seen, if nothing else for Ledger's Joker. The effects and the pace eclipse Batman Begins, rival Burton and, coupled with a storyline as dark as the original comics, this has got to be a contender for film of the year. Just not for all time.

Review Title: Legendary Superhero Masterpiece is Still The Best Of It's Kind
Review: The Dark Knight is Christopher Nolan's timeless magnum opus and a gripping, unforgettable thrill ride from start to finish. The acting preformances in this film are truly as great as they come. Heath Ledgers imfamous take on the Joker is undoubtedly one of the most captivating, disturbing, and iconic villain preformances in film history. All of the other main players in the film (especially Batman, Harvey Dent, and Commisioner Gordon) are also acted remarkably well, due in part to the immense strength of the film's cast.The action and stuntwork in this film are utterly spectacular. Few other films have ever managed to keep me on the edge of my seat this much during chases, and fight scenes. There are a number of reasons for this. Christopher Nolan clearly put a lot of work into the stunts in this film and it shows. Every stunt feels as if it is really happening and that you are there witnessing it with the characters. The music is undoubtedly some of the best in film history. The all time great film composer Hans Zimmer once again proves to be a master of his craft here, delivering a thoroughly blood pumping and epic musical score that enhances the action ten fold. The masterful cinematography and visual style of the film also further helps to enhance the stunning action.The film' s storytelling is some of the best in the history of blockbuster filmaking. It is dark, unforgettable, and exceptionally intricate. The film tackles very mature themes that are far beyond most comic book movies, and the characters are ALL masterfully well written. Many of the characters, such as Harvey Dent, Commisoner Gordon, and Batman, embark on some of the greatest and most thought provoking character arcs in modern film history. The richly detailed world building surrounding Gotham city also helps to make the film feel remarkably immersive (especially for a superhero movie).Overall the Dark Knight is without a doubt one of the greatest films of the last century and an essential film experience, even for those who are not fans of the superhero genre.

Dark, yes, complex, ambitious. Christopher Nolan and his co-writer Jonathan Nolan deserve a standing ovation. I don't usually go for loud movies filled with mindless gore and violence. "The Dark Knight" is certainly loud and violent but it's not mindless. It has depth and soul. Even the Joker, in an extraordinary creation by Heath Ledger, is deeply human. The natural petulance of Christian Bale makes his ego and alter ego the most fascinating and complex of all film superheroes. Part of the genius of this movie is that Batman himself, in screen time, is not really the lead. My attention was captivated by Heath Ledger and he determines and inspires the breathtaking atmosphere that envelopes Gotham as well as us. The aplomb of Christopher Nolan as a director is mind blowing and his secret, I believe, is his obvious respect for his audience. What he's done is to elevate a popular genre into Shakesperean proportions. Bravo!

Review Title: I never want to watch another movie again.
Review: Because it will be lacking.The Dark Knight was one of, if not THE best movie I've ever seen. I know people throw that around a lot after just seeing something, but I absolutely mean it.It's in that league with Empire Strikes Back. It's incredibly well written and acted, it looks beautiful, and it does things that no superhero movie before it has had the balls to do.The story has many, many layers but it never seems cluttered, and none of it ever feels unnecessary. Even the supporting characters have actual, meaningful story arcs, especially Jim Gordon and Harvey Dent.There are so many moments in it pulled from different Batman stories from over the years, either verbatim or slightly rearranged. I won't get into what they are as to not spoil anything for anyone who hasn't seen it yet, but fans who know their history and are paying attention will be VERY happy.Earlier I said that this movie does things that no superhero movie has had the balls to do, one of the biggest ones have a lot of scenes of our hero out of the costume. There is just as much if not more Bruce Wayne than Batman in this movie, and not for once does it feel like a bad thing. That's because he's actually using that time wisely and doing some real detective work, which is another first for a Batman movie. It's a shame that that's taken so long.I could get into how it's more of a crime drama than a superhero movie, which it is, but there are plenty of reviews out there that put that much more eloquently than I'll be able to. I will say that it was awesome to see a villain whose plan was more than "kill a bunch of people/hold the city hostage".Speaking of villains, Heath Ledger was absolutely jaw dropping. I sincerely hope anyone who was disappointed in his casting is eating their words right now. He IS the Joker. From now on when I read Batman comics, I will hear is voice for the Joker. That's not to take anything away from Aaron Eckhart, who plays Harvey Dent/Two Face, because he was perfect. You really feel for him, and that guy has made a lifelong fan here.Christian Bale is awesome as expected, as are Michael Caine, Gary Oldman, and Morgan Freeman. Thank god for Maggie Gyllenhaal, because I wouldn't be able to stand anymore Katie Holmes. Christian Bale really has all the aspects of Bruce Wayne nailed. He really gets that he's playing three characters. Batman, the real Bruce, and the irresponsible public Bruce. He has such a great presence and weight to his performance.I really, really can't get into the story here, because I don't want to spoil anything, and also I'm still trying to process it. If anyone wants to discuss just message me.In no particular order (mainly because I need to view TDK more times, and I'm tired): Empire Strikes Back Godfather pt II The Dark Knight.yeah it's that good.

In its ten years of existence the "Monsters on Vacation" franchise managed to become a national hit, and its characters could be remembered not only by children, but also by parents. The cartoon series broke the classic notions about the characters of famous monsters and was a kind of satire on our troubled world. The famous animator Gennady Tartakovsky imagined the lifestyles of every monster as strongly reminiscent of human life, and so the situations of monsters and humans were similar: the head of a large family, Wolfych, was tired of work, and Murray the Mummy could not figure out the intricacies of romantic relationships.The main storyline was a family conflict between the vampire daughter who fell in love with an ordinary man, and her father, Count Dracula, who seemed too strange beloved. Raising topical themes made the first monster cartoon a success, which led to the release of several sequels. And if the second part held the bar of quality of the first film, the third became a failed sequel, which has lost the spirit of the first parts. The news that not only a fourth film would follow, but also a short film about pets, was hardly accompanied by hope for resurrection: it became clear that nothing good awaited this series anymore. "Transformation" was a kind of finale of the whole series, summing up the results of the previous parts. The plot centers again on a dispute between Dracula and his son-in-law Johnny, this time concerning the inheritance of the Hotel Transylvania itself, which Drac wants to leave to his children and retire. Johnny's succession is questionable: a popular place among monsters could be ruined in an instant. To gain the hotel owner's trust, Johnny decides to take the bold step of transforming himself into a monster with Van Helsing's magic beam. However, something goes wrong, and not only does Johnny become a monster, but Drac also becomes a human. To find an antidote, they must travel around the world together and finally find common ground. "Monsters on Vacation: Transformation" is a film that is unlucky in almost every way. First of all, it is worth noting that the film was supposed to be released last summer, but it was postponed for several months, and then it went straight to the online services. Another Sony animated film, Mitchells vs. Machines, had a similar fate, which only played to the cartoon's advantage. The problem of the impact of technology on human life was reflected in the real world, because many people watched the film on their gadgets. Here the situation is almost the opposite: "Monsters on Vacation: Transformation" is an adventure cartoon for viewing in cinemas during the hot summer vacations.It was also unlucky that the creator of the first parts, Gennady Tartakovsky, did not find the time to fully approach work on the final franchise. In "Transformation", he acted only as a screenwriter, and the duo of Derek Drimon and Jennifer Klusky (the authors of the short film about the pets who live in the hotel "Transylvania") were appointed as directors. Therefore, and jokes built on the visual uniqueness of the world, in the new part disappeared. And in general "Monsters on Vacation: Transformation" can hardly be called funny: the satire on the modern world is gone, and instead there are scenes about how the strong personality of Dracula is trying to break the conditions of the human world.The new part also lacked the charm of the main characters. Almost the entire old cast of monsters turned into pathetic caricatures: the Mummy took the image of an old man falling asleep on the move, and Frank became a brutal narcissist who brags about his muscles. There are also problems with the script itself, which simply brings nothing new to the table. The conflict between Dracula and Johnny from the first parts made its way into the fourth with little change: the differences between the characters were again an occasion for family arguments that only Mavvis is able to resolve. The lack of a field for new solutions became a tugboat for the development of old lines, so the transformation itself had no effect on the characters: Johnny is still a choleric, and Drac is a grouch who wants to find idyll in everything.The finale seems to bring the characters to the point where the picture began. Trusting Johnny, Drac gives the young couple the opportunity to rebuild the ruined Hotel Transylvania, but the youngsters create the same building, only changing the decor inside. Perhaps in this there are similarities with the cartoon itself, which remained a copy of the first parts, never becoming a logical finale for the entire franchise.

Batman has proved successful in cleaning up the streets and a fresh new DA, Harvey Dent, is keen to clean up the mobsters in one big conspiracy case. Naturally an unpopular move, particularly with the psychotic villain known as "The Joker", who makes it his mission to unveil the identity of the Batman, before killing him. The Joker begins his reign of terror, forcing the citizens of Gotham to wonder whether or not it was worth having a Batman if this is the sort of chaos that his presence unleashes. With the stakes raised higher than ever, Bruce Wayne struggles to hold onto his moral code in the face of villain whose only aim is to unleash chaos and panic across the city.

If you're going to the The Dark Knight expecting a comic book movie or an action hero you might be disappointed because that's not what Christopher Nolan has created here. This is an extremely well-written film, with characters that pose social and psychological questions. It is also, in my opinion, the film with the best villain ever - The Joker. Even with all the hype you've heard about this, I can't begin to describe how blown away I was by Heath Ledger's performance. The cinematography couldn't have been better and it literally is a dark film. Hans Zimmer's contribution to this film was amazing. As always, he manages to create such unique music that perfectly fits this movie. Michael Cain's performance fits perfect within the movie. Morgan Freeman is always a pleasure to see on screen and he always brings a breath of fresh air to this intense film. Gary Oldman's talent needs no further praise, since he has proved on many occasions what a great actor he is.To be honest, I can't imagine why someone wouldn't like this film. If you're looking for action, you're going to get it. If you're looking for great acting, it doesn't really get any better. If you're a comic book fan, you'll thank Christopher Nolan for showing you new things about you favorite character. And if you're just going to the movies, I repeat, this is a great script, this is storytelling at its best. The only reason why you might not like this movie is if you got used to the highway chasing, car exploding, "multi-talented" - Michael Bay. Actually, Dark Knight has chase scenes as well, but here, they're part of the story, they're not just there for the sake of blowing up some cars. Explosions, another well-explored matter by the "great" Michael Bay... Dark Knight has explosions, hell, the one they shot in London got the locals calling the police to report a terrorist act. BUT the difference is, Dark Knight is about story and character, the visual effects (which are mind blowing) are there to support this.I hope you all enjoy The Dark Knight as much as I did.

Review Title: Really good and fun movie to watch
Review: The Dark Knight gives something new on the table, it has great story with excellent acting, visuals are outstanding. Joker Portrayed by Heath Ledger was a big surprise. His performance was perfect. This movie is more realistic then any other comic book movie. Big credit for Christian Bale. He is the only man that can say "I'm Batman", because he is Batman. Only problem in this movie is Bales "Batman" voice, it's more annoying then scary and powerful. This movie is more inspired then adapted by Batman comics. Everyone in this movie is awesome. Like I said, this movie brings something new on the table. RIP Heath Ledger. The key performance in the movie is by the late Heath Ledger, as the Joker. His Joker draws power from the actual inspiration of the character in the silent classic "The Man Who Laughs" (1928). His clown's makeup more sloppy than before, his cackle betraying deep wounds, he seeks revenge, he claims, for the horrible punishment his father exacted on him when he was a child. In one diabolical scheme near the end of the film, he invites two ferry-loads of passengers to blow up the other before they are blown up themselves. Throughout the film, he devises ingenious situations that force Batman (Christian Bale), Commissioner Gordon (Gary Oldman) and District Attorney Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart) to make impossible ethical decisions. By the end, the whole moral foundation of the Batman legend is threatened.

Some major parts of Batman's character is lost.Batman's always been the character stuck between his morals and what's necessary. In The Dark Knight, I don't even think Batman thought about killing The Joker. I guess he was too busy dealing with people dieing to think about saving them? It just doesn't seem to be a problem for him.Batman's also always been the character fighting in the shadows, so that both his audiences and the villains are left in suspense as to where he is. As I said earlier, in The Dark Knight you can see everything at all points in time during action scenes.

Review Title: The Best Comic Book Movie Ever? Think Again...
Review: I played hooky from work to see this film. I was so excited, I couldn't wait. I sat in my seat with avid anticipation. From the moment the film began, I couldn't take my eyes off the screen. It was riveting.Firstly, the story was so complex, offering twists and turns in the story and various subplots interwoven, it was obvious that this is not a straight-forward comic book film. The dialogue was expertly written and there was never a scene in which you roll your eyes & say "yeah, right." There was not a wasted frame, a useless scene or character. Everything you saw was intrinsic to the story.In the other Batman films, there has always been a sense of "cartoonish-ness," even in the first two films, as good as they were. In DK, there was none of this. Everything was based in a strong sense of realism, that what you were seeing could actually be happening somewhere. In the first films, there were also characters who were there to fill up the frame, IE: Comm. Gordon, whose sole function seemed to be to flip the switch on the Bat-signal. There was none of that to be found in this film. Every character had a role, an end to be achieved; a raison d'etre, if you'll pardon my French. And every actor performed it flawlessly. I'm not going to break down the performances individually, that's been done in previous critiques and for me to regurgitate stuff with which I heartily agree would be redundant.Suffice it to say, that to call "The Dark Knight" the best comic book movie ever made would cheapen it, pigeon-hole it into one tiny genre and I believe it deserves more than that. When the credits rolled at the end of this theatrical presentation, the entire audience stood and applauded. I own a copy of the Godfather trilogy and love those movies, so for all of you Brando/Pacino fans, I mean no disrespect, but in my humble opinion, this is the best, most perfect film ever made.

When I watch this movie each time I feel like Ledger is staring at me through the screen, his piercing eyes show the soul of the Joker & this was & will always be his best work.Lastly for Aaron Eckhart this was a little different to his style of movies I have previously seen him in. Review Title: The Best MOVIE That I Have Ever Seen
Review: I thought Batman Begins was a very well conceived and put together movie. We finally get Batman as a fully rendered character. We gain new insight into his motivations and the variables he must contend with in his role as protector of Gotham. We get to see Gary Oldman as an honest-to-goodness good guy. And we get to see Liam Neeson conducting perhaps his strangest facial hair experiment yet. But after seeing The Dark Knight, Batman Begins will forevermore be viewed (by me at least) as a handy little prologue to a FRICKIN' MASTERPIECE of a superhero film. To say it's the deepest mainstream comic adaptation ever produced would be akin to calling the Nolan/Ledger Joker 'a bit eccentric'. While watching it, I found myself thinking it was very long, which is usually a sign that it's TOO long, and therefore boring. But that's not actually the case here. The script is bulging with ideas, philosophical musings, THEMES, which Christopher Nolan is not content to gloss over in favor of cool set-pieces (as many comic adaptations are), but wants to explore, wants to allow the characters to explore, at a logical pace. So, what I guess I'm saying is, considering what it sets out to do, the movie is long ENOUGH, while still constantly holding the viewer's interest. And that's not to say the thematic exploration comes at the EXPENSE of big action, either. On the contrary, there is some truly awesome stuff going on here. The chase with the truck, for example, is fantastic, and there's some great hand-to-hand stuff too. But what engages us most is the characters, and, while the script is brilliant (the dialogue is sharp, and quite funny for the first two-thirds, before the drama really kicks in), this mainly comes down to the cast. Christian Bale. Taller than Michael Keaton was. More menacing than Val Kilmer was. Less like Adam West than George Clooney was. Solid and committed as always. He gives the character LIFE, and actually makes us feel for him. The word 'tortured' keeps coming to mind...and I suppose it's pretty appropriate. Heath Ledger. Y'know, I'd heard talk of an Oscar nomination, and thought it sounded a bit dubious. A Batman villain? Winning an Oscar? Is that what it's come to? Then I thought, is it because he didn't get one for Brokeback? Or more dubious still...is it because he...died? But...well...how can I put it...? It seems a bit blasphemous to compare Jack Nicholson to Cesar Romero, but after seeing Heath at work...Jack (who once seemed so awesome) just looks...well...lame. If you've seen it, you hopefully get what I mean. If you haven't...you need to. You will discover the true definition of commitment. Maggie Gyllenhaal. I didn't have any problem with Katie in the first one (at the time), but I doubt she could have pulled off the more emotional stuff Rachel goes through here. Seeing recasting was necessary (does Tom have a problem with his wife being involved with Batman? Too many bad memories perhaps? Why am I even talking about such garbage here?) they could have done a butt-load worse than Maggie. She rocks. As does Aaron Eckhart. But I'm not giving ANYTHING away. Suffice it to say my mind was blown...AGAIN. Makes Tommy Lee Jones look like...you get the idea. Michael Caine. Still one of my favorite actors. Alfred is the Shir. Morgan Freeman. Morgan Freeman. AOK. Gary Oldman. As in BB, no mania. No psychosis. No nervous tics. Absolute subtlety. Manages to hold his own alongside Christian, Heath and Aaron without resorting to parlor tricks. Sign of spectacular talent. Go Gaz. Eric Roberts! William Fichtner! Michael Jai White! Tiny Lister! The whole thing is just a big bag of thoughtful, well-executed entertainment. It's equal parts cerebral and visceral. Ideas and action. I've liked every Batman movie so far (okay, besides Batman & Robin), but this one makes them all look pretty bloody ordinary.

The Dark Knight- Heath Ledger Everyone will see "The Dark Knight" and awe in sheer unaltered amazement in the beauty of the darkness of this film in so many levels. I cannot help but remind myself as I watched that the true impact of the film is made all the more powerful and enduring with the true essence of an artist who left it all on the page. Heath Ledger as The Joker is so menacing and raw; that you cannot wonder and wish to see it again and again and again until you realize that in some way that The Joker via Heath is a mirror image of one own self destructive behaviors and tendencies. "The Dark Knight" is a pun on so many themes and nuances throughout the film. I myself a lover of story; stories about the human condition; stories about the essence of life; the story about the truth of our true selves we as humans are taught to hide from themselves. The Joker knows who he is and makes no apologizes about it. He challenges the nay sayers who feel they can control the truth within the soul. I was completely captivated by the challenge! The Joker is provoking The City of Gotham through its heroes to see its true self; embrace it whether it is light or dark or some where in the middle; but take ownership of it and dive in. Perhaps I saw too much in the film. Maybe I am projecting my own thoughts a realization; of late; into the work on the screen before me. But watching this film in a dark theatre alone yes alone I was screening it for the public it was a moment of true clarity of the rawness life brings. The anger, the angst, the destruction, the power, unbridled and strong; pulled at those in caverns of the soul; it remind me that true artistry is not in the editing room; but in the soul. To Heath I say THANK YOU!I knew and prepared myself for the fact that the viewing of "The Dark Knight" was going to be a bittersweet experience; for it was going to be the second to last time I will see the absolute talent of Heath Ledger on screen (note: his last film is slated to be released July 2009). But somehow I felt transcended through the 2 hours and 45 minutes at the close I wanted more; and I couldn't verbalize why. I wished it went on for hours more!After some introspective I have come to the realization that the film's effect me so; for I wanted to see the humanity of The Joker as he was able to show us "the darkness before the dawn" in everyone else in the film. I crave the other side of the menacing Joker. I wanted to see the softness; was there any we will never know and we shouldn't know; The Joker was to be that outlandish and raw... he knew who he was.As I crave the other side in those around me in my day to day. I wish those individuals in my day to day; and I my self were embraced their true selves and make no apologizes for it! Many people will see "The Dark Knight" for it powerful blockbuster showmanship. But I found it as a quotation; not a commentary; on the human condition. It spoke volumes to my soul at all levels. In short; "The Dark Knight" doesn't disappoint!

Review Title: The Greatest Comic book film ever made. An iconic masterpiece of film making and a phenomenal triumph of story telling.

Review Title: Greatest Superhero Movie of All Time
Review: Rated: 9.4/10 Rounded to 9This movie is by far the best superhero movie of all time. It can be explained in one word... "awesome!". Not too many movies are as good as this one. Review Title: AN OK Movie Not That Great. Only watch it once
Review: Since the beginning of time mankind has been fascinated by the idea of a "Superhero." We've gone from Gladiators, to Prince Charming, to El Cid, and finally to a man who dresses up like a bat. The Dark Knight is one of the more overrated movies of all time in which, the Batman (Christian Bale) joins forces with District Attorney Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart) in order to take on Gotham City's Mob and The Joker (Heath Ledger). For the past few months, Batman and Dent have been hard at work putting Gotham City's crime lords behind bars. Unfortunately, all of their hard work is about to go to waste as an unnatural force is brewing, a force that can't help but laugh at the horror that he creates. Enter the Joker. The Joker turns Gotham City upside down. He takes down a mob bank, blows up a hospital, destroys the people's trust in Batman, and turns Dent into Harvey Two-Face another homicidal psychopath. Batman must find a way to stop the Joker and Two-Face before they destroy Gotham City. The original movie is most definitely better than this oneI give the Dark Knight 2.5/5 stars. On a positive note the movie had wonderful acting, excellent action scenes and great music. Ledger gives a truly marvelous performance as the Joker. He gives his character the maniacal air that makes the Joker one of the more special villains of all time. Although many aspects of the flick were good, there were many flaws to this movie as well. For starters the movie was way too long. Two hours and 32 minutes is an eternity to sit in a chair. A suitable ending would have been at the exploding hospital scene instead of the anticlimactic, dragged out finish that occurred 30 minutes later. Secondly there were way too many villains. I counted five in this movie. There was the Scarecrow, The Mob, Super Accountant Lau, Harvey Two-Face and of course the Joker. The significance of the villainy got bogged down by the over quantity of villains. The third mistake was the lighting. During the Dark Knight there are many moments where it is just too dark to see anything. It got very annoying after a while trying to decipher who was doing what. Lastly, Christian Bale was a really irritating Batman. When he talked as Batman it sounded like he had a sore larynx. The Dark Knight truly is an over-hyped movie. It is a decent flick not a classic one that could be watched over and over again. I recommend it to anyone who is only going to try and watch it just once, because the first time is truly better than the 2nd or 3rd time. This is not the greatest movie of all time. Its simply an OK movie.

This is, as one would predict from a superhero film, the classic battle of good and evil; what one does not expect is for much of the battle to become largely internal. The script deals with some heavy philosophical themes but still manages to throw in some action scenes and great character moments; surprisingly, none of the screenplay's elements detract from each other, but rather, enhance each other, the mark of Jonathon Nolan's true genius. This movie's great script is made even better through Christopher Nolan's superb direction and cinematography, as well as inspired performances, the most mystifying of course coming from the late Heath Ledger. Review Title: The gold standard for superhero movies.
Review: When Batman and Robin came out in 1997, it was the nadir of the Batman franchise, and for superhero movies as a whole. This was the second superhero franchise WB screwed over (They ruined Superman a decade earlier with A Quest for Peace.) and Marvel wasn't making movies back then. There was no way people would take Batman seriously again.Cut to 2005 and then up and coming director Christopher Nolan made Batman Begins, the dark and gritty reboot that we ALL needed. It focused on who Batman (Christian Bale) was both beneath and outside of the cape and cowl. Between the great writing, performances, directing and score, Batman Begins was an incredible superhero movie, and topping it would be hard.And yet, The Dark Knight did exactly that. If Batman Begins was A New Hope, then TDK is Empire Strikes Back (The Dark Knight Rises was probably Return of the Jedi in terms of quality). This movie took its characters to morally dark and ambiguous areas, upped the stakes and most importantly, introduced Nolan's version of the Joker (portrayed masterfully by the late Heath Ledger, RIP) who is widely regarded as one of the best cinematic villains alongside Darth Vader and Anthony Hopkins' Hannibal Lecter. Of course, the Joker was already a legendary villain by virtue of the comics, cartoon and Jack Nicholson's awesomeness in the 1989 Batman movie, but Ledger made this character his own. He wasn't trying to imitate Nicholson or Mark Hamill from the cartoon. He perfectly understood the character, what he was all about, how he saw the world, and gave his own performance based on that. That Oscar was well deserved.But even without the Joker, this movie is wonderful. The directing and pacing were on point (one does not simply get bored), the other performances were great as well (I dig the weird Batvoice, haha) the dialogue was smart (though hard to follow) and it looked and sounded good too (Hans Zimmer should have been nominated). A side note: Nolan is a champion of practical effects over CGI, and that's mostly what you see here. And they look fabulous. Seriously, this is my favorite movie of all time.Because it's my favorite movie though, I'm gonna have to be a bit too harsh on it. I have three nitpicks with this movie that can largely be ignored. First off, the fight choreography is a bit weird at times (Who fights with their ELBOWS?) Second, I'm not a huge fan of Rachel Dawes. She was okay, but okay is not enough for a movie of this caliber. Third of all, again, the dialogue can be a bit hard to follow at times.Overall, this is an absolutely incredible movie and is guaranteed to be a major influence on future filmmakers.

Review Title: The Dark Knight Review by: ME!
Review: The Dark Knight Review With a record of over $314.2 million in its first 10 days of its release, The Dark Knight is set to be one of the most pleasing films to have come out in the last decade. This behemoth of a movie has already broken the New Midnight, Opening Weekend, and I-Max Record. Director Christopher Nolan and his crew really out did themselves in every way imaginable by creating this extraordinary piece of film. This movie goes beyond its limitations as an ordinary PG-13 comic book superhero movie.Let me start off by stating that this is the darkest, most intense Batman film to have ever been released into the public eye. Not only is it dark, but its packed with multiple well thought out interlocking plots that actually take you beyond what you've ever seen before. The movie portrays the lives of three main characters, Batman (Christian Bale), Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), and The Joker (Heath Ledger). In the film, the crime bosses of Gotham city become more aware on how to deal with their troubles with the Batman by night, but they face new challenges during the day with the new District Attorney Harvey Dent. Mean while, The Joker promises the crime organization that killing the Batman is the only way they will be able to keep their business going on for good.Being a lengthy movie, running at almost two and a half hours, it keeps you locked in suspense and curiosity, wondering what is going to happen next to the individual characters within the story. The cinematography itself is out standing with certain sections of the film being shot in the highest resolution known as I-Max. Most modern movies these days consist of overdone CGI with infinite scenes behind a green screen. The Dark Knight veers off from all that showing its audience that a great movie does not have to be completely over taken by the world of computer-generated imagery.Coming into more focus with the actors, this film would have not been what it was if it wasn't for its extraordinary cast. Christian Bale pulled off yet again another outstanding performance, reprising his role as the masked vigilante Batman. Another great addition to the new film was actor Aaron Eckhart with his amazing performance as the charismatic District Attorney, Harvey Dent. Eckhart goes deep into the portrayal of his character as he turns from a good hearted man of Gotham to an emotionally distressed, cheated thug known as Two-Face. Along side these actors comes a man that shocked the entire world with his performance as the violent, comical, homicidal maniac known as The Joker. Actor Heath Ledger dominated his role in The Dark Knight, leaving audiences all across the world with dropped jaws and complete satisfaction. Every moment Heath Ledgers character appears in the story, the film takes a whole new level of intensity and seriousness. Unlike Jack Nicolson's portrayal of The Joker in the 1989 film, Heath Ledger brings a more sinister, no holds bar type of character, who's message throughout the entire film becomes very clear as the story unravels. Also in the film are actors Michael Caine, new comer Maggie Gyllenhaal, Gary Oldman and Morgan Freeman.Overall this movie definitely lived up to the hype. It was not only a great comic-book superhero movie, but an overwhelming thriller, crime drama that will for the most part be tattooed into the lives of all who watched it. This film has all the elements that classifies it as one of the greatest movies ever made in the history of film making. The Nolan brothers along side story writer David S. Goyer redefined the movie watching experience by a the longest yard and for that this film deserves an outstanding (11 out of 10) -Alex Llanio

Review Title: Excelency in Film Making and Heath Ledger
Review: Let's make this short: what a brilliant piece of art. I would say that the majority of people who went to see this movie was never expecting something like what they got by the end of the projection. It is true that Christopher Nolan is one of the finest film makers of the last decade not having a single stain on his curriculum, but make a masterpiece of a superhero movie, is just an outstanding achievement. Throughout the movie history we have been offered with some superb movies which will be remarkable on their achievements for a long, long time... and we would be talking about films like "The Godfather", "Schindler's List", "On The Waterfront", "The Hustler" amongst so many other, that stood out from the crowd by being a reflection of a fantastic work done by their creators and the actors. And to tell you the truth, and being conscious about the fact that we can't compare "The Dark Night" with "Apocalypse Now" or "Raging Bull", we have to give a standing ovation to Nolan's work. It is classic on some may aspects of its making and at the same time its a very complex and believe work for an action/superhero movie. The cinematography and the musical score are perfect, the script is phenomenal and of course, and we are getting to the core of this review, the cast is fantastic. The actors have not fault anywhere (although I think in Christian Bale's performance we can point some overacting), but Heath Ledger delivers a performance of a lifetime, and it was the performance of his lifetime, unfortunately. This severe disturbed anarchist is miles away from the clown portrayed by Jack Nicholson back in 1989. Everything about Ledger's performance is amazing and a magnificent achievement in acting - The Academy Award was much deserved. Obviously Heath Ledger was no Marlon Brando or Paul Newman, but now we cans top a think that he could have been someone like those two great actors. His role as Ennis del Mar in "Brokeback Mountain" was absolutely fantastic, but his job as the Joker was unbelievable. It was really a shame that this movie couldn't get a nomination for Best Picture... it really was.

First of all I'd like to state I'm a long time Batman fan... I've seen all the films in the theaters throughout the years and followed the character at least in passing since the about '87. I hated Batman Begins, for the casual movie goer I understood the appeal. It was a big, stupid action film full of poorly conceived pseudoscience and nonsensical plot contrivances. For my taste it deviated far too much from the source material and the nature of the characters(with the notable exception of Johnathan Crane)and I quickly dismissed this often light action show. That being said The Dark Knight is a step in the right direction. Ledger is very good in his portrayal of the Joker. Borderline outstanding. Is he up for the Oscar for his role? Well, given his untimely and unfortunate death its possible. Aaron Eckhart is also fantastic in his role. The film was indeed a necessary darker tone than Begins which I truly appreciated. However, there were still some fundamental flaws to this film that keep it from being anywhere near as great as the Michael Bay crowd would tell you it is. Rachel Dawes, while not as annoying as the self righteous crusader she was portrayed in the first film, is an utterly pointless character and only served the purpose of being a trite plot device in a forced love triangle. She really lacked any real substance or evoked any empathy. None of this was Gyllenhaal's fault, it was merely a poorly written character. The main problem of the film was Bale's Batman though. I was pulling for Bale to play Bruce Wayne since American Psycho hit. I thought he was born for the role and the disappointment I felt from Begins when he failed to live up to my expectations I immediately attributed to Goyer's fluff script. But I acknowledge my mistake now. Originally I thought,upon the announcement of casting, that Ledger couldn't play the Joker. Ledger can play the Joker, its Bale who cannot play Batman. The character was a complete non-entity in this film without confidence, strength, or passion. Essentially this is Bruce Wayne trying to ditch his Batman persona to the first good knight who steps into the public spot light because he can't bag his ex-girlfriend while he wears the cowl. It was borderline sickening and even more so now that the masses have swallowed this up as an accurate portrayal of a beloved character. Even Bale's Batman comes across as a one dimensional parody of a bully. Bale's voice hasn't much improved much in the sequel, bouncing between a slightly more hoarse version of Bruce Wayne's voice and an incoherent growl which leaves the audience wondering how, in the heat of the moment, anyone can really understand him. Those negatives aside one ends up with a solid outing that is slightly better shot than its predecessor although action sequences are still inconsistent and poorly choreographed. It is very much a villain driven piece that left at least me rooting for the monsters of the film to clean house on some of the more annoying "hero" characters. The final act of the film does leave a sour taste in the viewers mouth as it once again relies on a poorly contrived dues en machina scientific machine to save the day and a rather insignificant sacrifice out hero makes in light of the mass anarchy in the streets around him. This sacrifice is rather perplexing given that with the abundant confusion created by the Joker I, and the group I was with, were completely mystified why this character made this "sacrafice" and didn't blame events on the anarchy around them. Anyway, worth seeing for Eckhart and Ledger's performance and really rather good at points... but never that good.
